decisions.ruling: Build the quote gate now: an order on an instrument with no quote in the platform's market snapshot is refused and journaled. It reads presence only, because a freshness bound would be a new threshold that needs its own argued record (decision 7). Borrow stays fail-closed, every uncovered short refused, until qip-data-finder admits a licensed borrow source under ADR 0157; that source is a vendor and the owner's call, so the row stays PARTIAL.

Quotes land in the snapshot via market.snapshot.apply_quote (platform.rs ~12072), readable through qip-market snapshot.rs::get. qip_capital::margin::estimate_exit's quote_available/borrow_available arms have no production caller, and Platform::observe_borrow has no production caller. decisions.ruling: The capital-society coordinator is a step the kernel composes over qip-capital, not a new binary (ADR 0127). It settles proposals in the survival waterfall's order: liquidity and collateral first, funding obligations next, allocation last from what remains. A set that would sum past the region's grant is cut from the bottom, and no proposal ever widens a grant. The durable ledger stays on the current store until the Spanner deploy is funded, and nothing new is sized (decision 7).
decisions.rationale: No coordinator exists: grep for 'coordinator' in qip-capital (allocation.rs, funding.rs, collateral.rs, treasury.rs) and qip-kernel finds none. qip_capital::survival already fixes a priority waterfall: reserved cash, margin, collateral, settlement, funding maturity, hedge and stressed-liquidity reserve before opportunity capital. qip-kernel central/regions.rs:349 GrantManifests is the grant ledger to reconcile against. ADR 0127 makes capital brains crate boundaries the kernel composes. The precedence rule is a new capital-policy contract, hence an ADR first. It only narrows grants, so it tightens.
decisions.closure: After the ADR, add a kernel step that composes qip-capital's four proposers and settles them against GrantManifests in waterfall order, with test competing_proposals_never_sum_past_the_grant and a mutation that drops the cut.
decisions.adr_title: The capital-society coordinator is a kernel step that settles allocation, funding, liquidity and collateral proposals in the survival waterfall's order against the region's grant, and no set of proposals ever sums past it
decisions.skeptic: No 'coordinator' exists in qip-capital or qip-kernel src. survival.rs:7-17 fixes the waterfall. GrantManifests is at central/regions.rs:349. ADR 0127 exists. qip-kernel already depends on qip-capital (Cargo.toml:30), so no new dependency or ADR 0109 issue arises. The rule only cuts toward the grant and sizes no new budget, so it is consistent with decision 7. A precedence contract warrants ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT. One caveat for the ADR: the closure's 'qip-capital's four proposers' overstates the code. Only allocation.rs has StrategyProposal; funding.rs has plan_funding/FundingPlan, and collateral.rs and treasury.rs expose no proposal type. The ADR must define the four proposal shapes rather than assume them.

decisions.ruling: Capital agents are approved as proposers only. Each of the ten named agents submits a plan every cycle, and the kernel records all ten before it chooses. The plan it acts on is the per-line minimum of those plans and the one allocator's plan, so no agent can widen a grant and nothing new is sized (decision 7 holds). Until ADR 0153 gives tax an input, the tax-aware agent submits an abstention that names the missing input.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/services/qip-capital/src/allocation.rs::CapitalAllocator::allocate is the only decider. It is reached through backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/central/plane.rs::CentralPlane::allocate (:1729), and no CapitalPlan or capital-agent type exists anywhere in backend/crates. qip-capital already has treasury.rs, funding.rs, collateral.rs, margin.rs, survival.rs and exposure.rs for the agents to wrap. backend/crates/services/qip-capital-fabric/src/lib.rs refuses 'a second budget'. A minimum across plans can only narrow, so the leverage and funding agents cannot raise any risk limit. ADR 0153 d7 gives tax no input. Owner decision 7 of 2026-10-25 keeps one allocator and sizes nothing new.
decisions.adr_title: Capital agents only propose: every named agent's plan is recorded each cycle, and the kernel acts on the per-line minimum of those plans and the one allocator's
decisions.closure: After the ADR, add a CapitalPlan type and ten proposers in qip-capital built over the existing modules. Make CentralPlane::allocate record every plan for the cycle before it acts on the per-line minimum with CapitalAllocator::allocate's plan. Test that all ten plans are recorded before the choice and that a plan above the allocator's line is clipped (mutation: take the maximum).

decisions.ruling: Joint construction is approved as one run that can only narrow. construct_from takes grouped caps for strategies from the allocator's plan, for horizons from the reconciled horizon pools and for regions from the region ceilings already on record, and no cap may loosen the mandate. No asset-class budget and no new regional budget is sized here. Where no figure is on record, the cap is the book's own target gross, and a real number needs its own risk record with the numbers argued (decision 7).

Joining the three crosses three service contracts. Owner decision 7 of 2026-10-25 forbids sizing a new budget here.
decisions.adr_title: Joint construction is one optimiser run whose grouped caps only narrow the mandate, and no class or region budget is sized without its own risk record

decisions.ruling: No cloud worker pool is bought for autonomous development (decision 5). The autonomous-development plane is agent-sandbox.yml on ephemeral hosted runners. It already allows one run per lane, with a time budget and egress request and byte quotas. It gains a max_concurrent_lanes cap in the agent policy that the lane validator enforces, set no higher than the largest wave the committed manifest already runs. The Cloud Build private pool stays off.
decisions.rationale: .github/workflows/agent-sandbox.yml::concurrency (group agent-sandbox-${{ inputs.lane }}) limits each lane to one run but does not limit how many lanes run at once. scripts/agent-policy.json::sandbox caps each run at egress_max_requests 4000 and egress_max_bytes 4294967296. infrastructure/terraform/modules/build-pool/main.tf::google_cloudbuild_worker_pool.pool is off everywhere, behind the protected build-pool.tf. .github/workflows/deploy.yml::concurrency allows one deploy at a time per environment. Neither the runbook nor the row names a cost for a new pool. scripts/agent-policy.json and scripts/agent-lanes.mjs are protected paths, so the change ships as a patch for the owner to approve.
decisions.adr_title: The autonomous-development pool is the agent sandbox on ephemeral hosted runners, capped by a concurrent-lane limit the lane validator enforces, and no cloud worker pool is bought
decisions.closure: After the ADR, a protected patch adds sandbox.max_concurrent_lanes to scripts/agent-policy.json. scripts/agent-lanes.mjs validate then refuses any manifest whose wave exceeds the cap. Add a test pair: a wave over the cap is refused and the committed round-3 manifest is admitted. build-pool.tf is not touched and stays off.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. agent-sandbox.yml:65-66 uses the concurrency group agent-sandbox-${{ inputs.lane }}. agent-policy.json sandbox sets egress_max_requests 4000 and egress_max_bytes 4294967296, and lane_limits caps max_minutes. build-pool/main.tf:60 declares google_cloudbuild_worker_pool.pool behind cloud_build_private_pool_enabled = false. deploy.yml:78 is concurrency per environment. agent-policy.json and agent-lanes.mjs are protected, so shipping the change as an owner patch is right. agent-lanes.mjs validate already computes waves, and round-3.json's largest wave is 5 lanes. A cap adds a refusal and buys nothing. Caveat: the 11 lanes running under the 2026-10-31 decision 2 are not in round-3.json, so a cap of 5 binds only future manifests. The owner should set the value knowing it would refuse an 11-lane single wave.

decisions.decision: IMPLEMENT the modules/data plan run only. With enable_cloud_storage = true and a mock provider, it asserts google_storage_bucket.archive[0] has retention_policy is_locked and versioning enabled. Send the landing-to-archive clause through ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT, reconciled with R12-FABRIC-8101 and R12-DATA-8124: fabricd writes the regional landing, and a named copy step fills the locked archive (fabricd's own second write or a transfer). The row is STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY on the protected, billed enable_cloud_storage flip.
decisions.ruling: No transfer service is bought for the archive. Object lifecycle cannot move objects between buckets, so the landing clause is restated: the archive receives each sealed segment from fabricd's own archive path, never from a landing bucket. A plan shows the archive's locked retention and versioning. Storage stays off until the change that lands the first writer, because the seven-year lock cannot be undone.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/data/main.tf::google_storage_bucket.archive declares versioning and retention_policy is_locked = true behind enable_cloud_storage. ::google_storage_bucket.segments records that object lifecycle cannot move an object to another bucket. modules/data/tests/ has no plan run that reads is_locked or versioning. Only backend/crates/tests/qip-acceptance/tests/data_infrastructure_guards.rs::the_archive_bucket_retention_policy_is_locked_to_prevent_modification checks them, by scanning text. backend/crates/apps/qip-fabricd/src/config.rs::ARCHIVE_BUCKET already lets fabricd write the archive directly. billed-plan-2026-10-19.md finding 3 warns that the 2557-day lock is irreversible.
decisions.closure: Add a modules/data plan run with enable_cloud_storage = true. It asserts that google_storage_bucket.archive[0] has retention_policy is_locked and versioning enabled, beside the existing single-region refusal run. Record the restated clause in the row. The row stays PARTIAL until dev's enable_cloud_storage flip (protected, billed) and a real plan.
decisions.skeptic: The plan run is sound: with a mock provider it bills nothing. No existing test asserts is_locked or versioning, and the single-region refusal run exists at retention_classes.tftest.hcl:147. The restated landing clause rests on a misread. qip-fabricd config.rs documents ARCHIVE_BUCKET as 'The Cloud Storage landing bucket sealed segments are archived to (FABRIC-8101, DATA-8124)'. archive_target admits exactly one of ARCHIVE_DIR or ARCHIVE_BUCKET. R12-FABRIC-8101 requires content-addressed segments in regional landing buckets, then copied to the archive. R12-DATA-8124 requires a regional landing store written by fabric-archive. 'The archive receives each sealed segment from fabricd's own archive path, never from a landing bucket' therefore either drops the regional landing those two rows require, or needs fabricd to write twice. A dual write is a code and architecture change, not a one-line restatement under IMPLEMENT.

decisions.decision: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT, with the rule restated: a stream archives under its declared class, and a stream whose declared class is less durable than any topic it carries is refused at load. The rest of the closure is unchanged: class prefixes under ARCHIVE_PREFIX, transition-only rules with no Delete, module env wiring, and the two-class test.
decisions.ruling: Each fabric stream archives under the retention class its catalogue entry declares. A stream whose declared class disagrees with its topics' Topic::retention_class is refused at catalogue load. The new class prefixes get storage-class transitions and no delete rule, so nothing in the fabric archive is kept for less time than it is today.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/libs/qip-events/src/topic.rs::Topic::retention_class and backend/crates/libs/qip-storage/src/lake.rs::RecordClass meet the unit clause. backend/crates/libs/qip-storage/src/segment/archive.rs::ARCHIVE_SEGMENT_PREFIX ("segments/sha256/") and ::ARCHIVE_MANIFEST_PREFIX ("manifests/") fall outside the lake/class= lifecycle prefixes of infrastructure/terraform/modules/data/main.tf::google_storage_bucket.archive. infrastructure/event-fabric/streams.local.json already declares a retention class per stream. backend/crates/apps/qip-fabricd/src/config.rs reads ARCHIVE_BUCKET and ARCHIVE_PREFIX, but modules/event-fabric-broker passes neither. The archive layout belongs to ADR 0156.
decisions.adr_title: A fabric stream archives under the retention class its catalogue declares, a stream whose topics disagree is refused at load, and no class prefix gains a delete rule
decisions.closure: After the ADR, make Broker::archive_sealed write under <prefix>/class=<retention>/ using the stream's catalogue retention. Pass QIP_EVENT_FABRIC_ARCHIVE_BUCKET and _PREFIX from modules/event-fabric-broker. Add transition-only lifecycle rules for those prefixes in modules/data. Test that tick-journal and own-fill segments archive under different classes (mutation: one prefix for all). The tfvars flips and the apply stay the owner's.
decisions.skeptic: The refusal as worded rejects the committed catalogue. infrastructure/event-fabric/streams.local.json stream reflex-journal.local declares retention event_anchored but carries reflex.fabric_gap. qip-events topic.rs maps EventFabricGap to RetentionClass::Irreplaceable (in the arm with ReflexOutcomeRecorded, ReflexChainSpan and LedgerOperationRecorded). The same topic also sits in reflex-outcomes.local as irreplaceable. 'A stream whose declared class disagrees with its topics' Topic::retention_class is refused at catalogue load' would stop fabricd loading the shipped catalogue. Archiving by stream class would also label irreplaceable gap records with the 90-day rolling event_anchored class. The other citations hold: the archive.rs prefixes segments/sha256/ and manifests/, the lake/class= lifecycle rules, modules/event-fabric-broker passes no ARCHIVE variable, and ADR 0156 governs the layout.

After that ADR, build the load job and staged OutcomeSink, and wire QIP_BIGQUERY_* only where enable_cloud_storage and enable_bigquery are both true. If 0182 is kept instead, build its fabricd consumer, and the row is STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY on event_fabric_broker.
decisions.ruling: BigQuery is fed by batch load from Cloud Storage, not by a fabric sink. fabricd has no boot image, while a load needs only the two storage switches already declared. OutcomeSink stops streaming rows: it stages outcome files under an expiring prefix and loads them. No streaming insert remains on any shipped path.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/services/qip-mesh/src/bigquery.rs carries insertAll only, with no load job. backend/crates/apps/qip-deepbrain/src/warehouse.rs::OutcomeSink streams rows directly. The isolation tests in backend/crates/tests/qip-acceptance/tests/architecture.rs already hold: no_edge_cell_can_hold_a_handle_to_the_warehouse_or_the_wide_column_store and no_crate_on_the_reflex_path_can_reach_the_bigquery_client. event_fabric_broker is null in every environment and fabricd has no boot image. The GCS path needs only enable_cloud_storage and enable_bigquery.
decisions.closure: Add a load-job call to qip-mesh/src/bigquery.rs. Make qip-deepbrain warehouse::OutcomeSink stage outcomes under an expiring modules/data prefix and load them, instead of calling insertAll. Wire QIP_BIGQUERY_* in catalogue.tf. Test that no shipped path calls insertAll (mutation: restore the streaming call). Deployment waits on the two storage switches.
decisions.skeptic: The ruling contradicts an accepted ADR it does not cite. ADR 0182 decision 4 (Accepted 2026-10-25): 'The warehouse write path stays insertAll (DATA-10081) ... The remaining code is a fabricd consumer driving the warehouse.' The ruling removes insertAll from every shipped path, adds a test that forbids it, and rejects the fabric sink. That reverses 0182 decision 4 by code under IMPLEMENT and blocks R12-DATA-10081's planned sink. That is an architecture or contract change and needs an ADR first. Separately, wiring QIP_BIGQUERY_* in catalogue.tf while dev has enable_bigquery = true and enable_cloud_storage = false would point OutcomeSink at a staging bucket that does not exist. The wiring must be conditional on both switches. The isolation tests the ruling cites exist (architecture.rs:1053, :3206), and qip-mesh bigquery.rs has insertAll only.

decisions.ruling: An oracle's report never resolves a market by itself. discover proposes a resolution only when the market's own criteria, evaluated over named observations from its named source, agree with the report. A market with no such observation stays pending. The plane stays off until a licensed event source is catalogued (ADR 0151 decision 10).
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/event_markets.rs::EventMarketPlane::discover passes PredictionUpdate::Report straight to MarketResolution::observe (:503). backend/crates/services/qip-prediction/src/market.rs::EventMarket::evaluate (:429) and resolution.rs::Observations have no caller outside tests. oracle.rs::OracleReport carries only an outcome, a confidence and free-text evidence. ADR 0151 d10 opens the plane only with a licensed source, and QIP_DEEPBRAIN_BREADTH_PLAN is unset in every environment. Adding the refusal tightens the path.
decisions.closure: In EventMarketPlane::discover, run EventMarket::evaluate over adapter-delivered Observations before MarketResolution::observe, and refuse a report that contradicts the criteria or has no observation. Add the test 'an oracle report contradicting the market's own criteria is refused and the market stays pending' (mutation: skip the evaluate check). The row stays PARTIAL until a licensed event source is catalogued.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. event_markets.rs:503 passes PredictionUpdate::Report straight to resolution.observe. EventMarket::evaluate (market.rs:429) has no non-test caller. OracleReport carries only outcome, confidence, reported_at and evidence. ADR 0151 decision 10 (:106-108) opens the event plane only with a licensed source and reads outcomes from named observations from a named source. QIP_DEEPBRAIN_BREADTH_PLAN appears in no infrastructure file. Refusing a report that lacks agreeing observations is a pure tightening inside the kernel's own plane. Keeping the row PARTIAL until a licensed source is catalogued is the conservative reading. Kernel tests that resolve markets by report alone will need observation fixtures, which does not weaken them.

decisions.ruling: A replay environment is wanted, and the requirement is not restated to the in-process replay. Replay is declared as a fifth environment under ADR 0118 and left off, like test, stage and prod. It is admitted only with observation autonomy, no execution node, no venue credential and reader-only grants on curated data. No project is billed until the deploy is paid for (decision 5).
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/variables.tf::variable.environment admits only dev, test, stage and prod. infrastructure/gitops/gates/replay/freight.yaml is a Kargo gate with no project, and R12-GCP-10143 graded replay as an environment-less stage (backend/crates/tests/qip-acceptance/tests/gitops.rs::every_blueprint_stage_maps_to_an_environment_directory_or_a_documented_environment_less_stage). backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/replay.rs replays only in-process. infrastructure/foundation already declares test, stage and prod as off at no cost. variables.tf and environments/** are protected paths, so the change ships as a patch. Every existing environment keeps its validation unchanged, and the new value comes with stricter refusals.
decisions.adr_title: Replay is a fifth environment, declared and off, admitted only with observation autonomy, no execution node, no venue credential and reader-only grants on curated data
decisions.closure: After the ADR 0118 amendment, a protected patch admits replay in variables.tf only with preconditions that refuse any ceiling above observation, any execution node, any venue secret and any writer grant on curated data. It adds environments/replay/terraform.tfvars and a declared-off foundation project. Add a plan harness pair that refuses an execution node and admits the read-only configuration. Check that the longest resource id built from 'replay' stays within the 30-character service-account limit.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. variables.tf:57 admits only dev, test, stage and prod. infrastructure/gitops/gates/replay exists. gitops.rs:7529 holds the environment-less-stage test, and CHAIN/GATES (:73-76) list replay as a gate. foundation/terraform.tfvars declares test, stage and prod with enabled = false. The fifth environment is declared off and bills nothing. Its admission carries stricter preconditions than the existing four, whose validation is unchanged. variables.tf and environments/** go to the owner as a protected patch. Restating the requirement to the in-process replay would have redefined it to pass the row. Notes: amending accepted ADR 0118 needs a person (only new ADRs are agent self-reviewable), so write it as a new ADR that amends 0118. The gitops.rs CHAIN/GATES test will need the replay directory reconciled.

decisions.decision: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT. Title: "A print is raw, whether a central Tick or a Trade: the cognitive layer takes a price only as time-aligned state built at the ingestion seam, and the no-raw-tick guard refuses Tick, SensedRecord::Tick and SensedRecord::Trade". Closure: after the ADR, qip-market-ingestion folds SensedRecord::Tick and SensedRecord::Trade into interval state before Platform::observe. absorb_records loses its Tick arm and the Trade arm's world-model 'close' write. The ADR states whether the Trade, Quote and Book updates to the paper MarketSnapshot (used by the quote loop and paper fills) are execution-side and outside the cognitive guard, or are also moved. cognitive_no_raw_ticks.rs adds Tick, SensedRecord::Tick and SensedRecord::Trade to its refused names. A test pins the fusion input (qip-kernel fusion.rs) to MarketTrace/TracePoint. MarketStatePack follows ADR 0151 decision 2 under R12-CONTRACT-7072.
decisions.ruling: The central `Tick` is a raw print, and the cognitive layer does not take it. ADR 0151 decision 9 already says the centre has no clock discipline behind a `Tick`, so a `Tick` cannot be the time-aligned state the requirement names. Prices reach the kernel only as state built below it, and the guard refuses `Tick` by type. Reading it otherwise would redefine the requirement to pass the row.
decisions.rationale: The default path takes a raw print today. backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs::Platform::absorb_records (reached from Platform::observe) has a SensedRecord::Tick arm that writes each print's price as a 'close' feature. qip-market-ingestion connectors/coinbase_ticker.rs and synthetic/mod.rs emit SensedRecord::Tick on default paths. The guard backend/crates/tests/qip-acceptance/tests/cognitive_no_raw_ticks.rs::RAW_TICK_IDENTIFIERS and RAW_TICK_PATHS do not name qip_market::quote::Tick or SensedRecord::Tick, so a fn taking Vec<\Tick> passes it. The ADR is needed because the change alters Platform::observe's input contract, and ADR 0151's 'Code it constrains' lists Tick as unchanged. Adding the names to the guard tightens it.
decisions.adr_title: The central Tick is a raw print: the cognitive layer takes a price only as time-aligned state built at the ingestion seam, and the no-raw-tick guard refuses Tick and SensedRecord::Tick
decisions.closure: After the ADR, qip-market-ingestion folds SensedRecord::Tick into interval state before Platform::observe. Platform::absorb_records loses its Tick arm. cognitive_no_raw_ticks.rs adds Tick and SensedRecord::Tick to its refused names. A test pins the tick desk's fusion input to MarketTrace/TracePoint. MarketStatePack follows ADR 0151 decision 2 under R12-CONTRACT-7072.
decisions.skeptic: The scope misses half the code. platform.rs::absorb_records has a SensedRecord::Trade arm at line 12172 with the same shape as the Tick arm: it writes each trade print's price into the world model as a 'close' feature (its comment says "a trade is exactly that"). Trades reach Platform::observe on default paths: synthetic/mod.rs:442 maps trades into SensedRecord::Trade (the same file the rationale cites for Tick), and rest.rs:623 is qip-fastbrain's RestMarketDataAdapter. The closure removes only the Tick arm, and the guard adds only Tick and SensedRecord::Tick. So after the change the kernel still takes a raw print on its default path, a fn taking Vec<Trade> still passes cognitive_no_raw_ticks.rs, and the ruling's "prices reach the kernel only as state built below it" is false the day it lands. The direction is right and it only tightens, but the ADR has to cover every per-print arm.
decisions.decision_detail: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT. Title: "A print is raw, whether a central Tick or a Trade: the cognitive layer takes a price only as time-aligned state built at the ingestion seam, and the no-raw-tick guard refuses Tick, SensedRecord::Tick and SensedRecord::Trade". Closure: after the ADR, qip-market-ingestion folds SensedRecord::Tick and SensedRecord::Trade into interval state before Platform::observe. absorb_records loses its Tick arm and the Trade arm's world-model 'close' write. The ADR states whether the Trade, Quote and Book updates to the paper MarketSnapshot (used by the quote loop and paper fills) are execution-side and outside the cognitive guard, or are also moved. cognitive_no_raw_ticks.rs adds Tick, SensedRecord::Tick and SensedRecord::Trade to its refused names. A test pins the fusion input (qip-kernel fusion.rs) to MarketTrace/TracePoint. MarketStatePack follows ADR 0151 decision 2 under R12-CONTRACT-7072.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0148 decided this on 2026-10-19 and it stands. A missed opportunity is a claim graded in basis points over its own horizon, and it is never priced at a side nobody proposed. What is not graded is counted, never zeroed. No new design is needed, only the build that record already calls for.
decisions.rationale: The row's gap predates ADR 0148, which names R12-TICK-2077 in decisions 1-2. Those decisions have not landed in code. backend/crates/services/qip-twin/src/capture.rs::Action::MissedOpportunity still reads 'the variant the audit flagged as missing' and does not say it has no producer by decision. No qip_opportunities_unpriced_total counter exists anywhere in backend/crates. Grading already runs: platform.rs record_prediction is called before approve-or-reject, calibrate_resolved does not filter on approval, and DecisionTaken::RejectedOnReview is resolved with EpisodeOutcome::realised_move_bps. qip-kernel tests/episodic.rs proves that a veto episode is recorded. It does not prove the grade reads only the decision-time view.
decisions.closure: Rewrite Action::MissedOpportunity's doc comment to say it has no producer and to name ADR 0148. Add qip_opportunities_unpriced_total{reason} in the kernel, with the closed enum labels expired_unworked, no_mechanism and undirected_claim. Add a qip-kernel learning test: a hypothesis rejected on review resolves to realised_move_bps from the view fixed at decision time, and the test fails if the view reads later bars. Restate the row's text to ADR 0148.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. ADR 0148 decisions 1-2 name R12-TICK-2077, decide the rule and define the counter with its three closed labels. capture.rs:82 still reads "The variant the audit flagged as missing". No qip_opportunities_unpriced_total exists in backend/crates. calibrate_resolved (platform.rs:21006) filters on is_open and resolves_at only, not on approval. DecisionTaken::RejectedOnReview is at platform.rs:15831, and qip-kernel/tests/episodic.rs exists. Nothing needs a deployment or a third party, no limit is touched, and no protected path is involved. One wording fix for the lane: the realised move has to read the observation at the horizon. What must be fixed at decision time is the reference value and the claim. The test should fail if the reference or the claim is taken from bars after the decision, not whenever any later bar is read.

Also an inspection test that maps every scope item to a composition-root path and a named test. That test can be written now for the shipped items, and it fails by name on the unlicensed ones.
decisions.skeptic: Outcome is correct. KNOWN_SOURCES (connector_feed.rs:51-59) holds exactly the seven sources the ruling names. ADR 0157:360 lists TICK-1175 as 'BILLED vendor choice; options are refused on the evidence of ADR 0050', and :402 records four option publishers read and refused. Vendor choice and reading terms belong to the owner. The rationale has two errors, and neither changes the outcome. (a) Cell::set_funding_rate is called only in tests, but those are the #[cfg(test)] module of edge/qip-edge/src/cell.rs (:13573, :13610 after :12739) and funding.rs unit tests, not edge/qip-edge/tests/cell.rs. (b) qip-chain is more than typed models. src/rpc.rs::JsonRpcChainAdapter opens a socket and captures blocks and pending transactions. It is composed by no root, only qip-acceptance e2e_live.rs. So the on-chain gap is a licensed node endpoint plus root composition, not a new connector. The closure should reuse JsonRpcChainAdapter and qip-market-ingestion depth.rs::DepthFeedAdapter. The inspection test must not land red in CI. Write it with a named pending list of unlicensed items that fails if the list and the tree disagree.

decisions.ruling: Crypto order books, perpetual funding, liquidations, dealer rate quotes, and mempool and venue state are not captured until each has an ADR 0157 licence record. That holds even for a free public feed: it enters only as a record that quotes the terms it was read from. No agent accepts a venue's terms in my name. The row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: qip-market-ingestion src/connectors/coinbase_ticker.rs is spot ticker only. ecb_key_rates.rs and nyfed_effr.rs are policy reference rates, not dealer quotes. src/connector_feed.rs::KNOWN_SOURCES has no order-book, funding or liquidation source. qip_edge::funding::FundingRate has no capture path; Cell::set_funding_rate is called only from tests. qip-chain src/mempool.rs and src/amm.rs have typed models but no connector. Under ADR 0157, vendor choice and licence reading are the owner's, and vendor choice is billed.
decisions.closure: Once each source is licensed under ADR 0157: a connector per feed under ConnectorFeed KNOWN_SOURCES, and a typed-record test per event type. Also replace the row's verification command (qip-twin --test twin), which tests none of this, with that inspection.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. coinbase_ticker is spot only. ecb_key_rates and nyfed_effr are policy rates. KNOWN_SOURCES has no book, funding or liquidation source. ADR 0157:362 lists TICK-2046 as 'BILLED vendor choice; crypto depth is the first candidate to read terms for', so refusing to accept terms even for a free feed matches the ADR. The register's verification really is 'cargo test -p qip-twin --test twin' (assessment/R12-M2.json), and it tests none of the named event types, so replacing it with the inspection is a tightening. Same correction as TICK-1175: the 'no connector' claim is partly a misread. qip-market-ingestion src/depth.rs::DepthFeedAdapter is a socket-opening order-book adapter, used only by qip-cli's demo and unwired per ADR 0157 (DATA-2005). qip-chain src/rpc.rs::JsonRpcChainAdapter captures pending transactions and blocks. The closure should compose these in a root once a source is licensed, not write new connectors. The outcome does not depend on the misread.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0156 §2.4 stands. read_indexed keeps proving the whole segment. No ranged read that trusts the manifest further is built on a cost nobody has measured. The deferral is revisited only on a committed measurement of hydrate bytes and latency per read_indexed on the running broker's replay path. The row stays PARTIAL until that measurement exists.
decisions.rationale: qip-storage src/segment/archive.rs::ArchiveReader::read_indexed and read_indexed_with_extent re-prove the whole segment's hash before serving a batch, and they cache the last hydrated segment (last_indexed). Manifest.replay_index holds only (offset, byte_start), so nothing exists that a fetched range could be checked against. ADR 0156 §2.4 and its Alternatives-rejected section refuse 'add the per-batch digest and ranged reads now' as a weaker proof without a measured need. .claude/rules/10-product-direction.md item 4 forbids weakening a guarantee for speed without saying so. Latency must be measured against the GCS archive on a deployed qip-fabricd broker, and dev is not running.
decisions.closure: After the dev deploy, commit hydrate bytes and latency per read_indexed from qip-fabricd's replay path against the GCS archive. Build only if that shows whole-segment cost beyond what a larger roll_after_bytes can remove. In that case, a record superseding ADR 0156 §2.4 adds the separately named ranged read that proves a batch digest, with a test that drives the real Archiver.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. archive.rs:685 read_indexed and :700 read_indexed_with_extent re-prove the whole segment. last_indexed (:617) caches the last hydrated segment. replay_index is Vec<(u64,u64)> (:209). ADR 0156 §2 item 4 (:125-142) builds the ranged read only on 'a committed measurement of hydrate bytes and latency per read_indexed on the broker's replay path'. Alternatives-rejected (:348) refuses 'add the per-batch digest and ranged reads now'. Keeping the stronger proof weakens nothing. Waiting on a measurement from a deployed broker against the GCS archive is a deployment dependency, so STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY is the right bucket. The closure honours §2.4's requirement for a new method with its own name.

decisions.ruling: Synthetic worlds may vary what no feed measures. Policy, weather, default and supply drivers get a synthetic-only producer. The branches they grow stay Provenance::Synthetic, and UNDERSTAND and REASON never read such a driver as evidence. A real producer for those kinds still waits on a source licensed under ADR 0157.
decisions.rationale: In qip-twin src/futures.rs, WorldDriver has only id, sensitivities and evidence, and no kind. FutureTree::grow varies only shock size, propagation and sign. The module doc already says 'a synthetic branch is never observed data' (Provenance::Synthetic). qip-simulation-engine src/market.rs::SyntheticMarket and src/agents.rs vary participants, liquidity and structure. ADR 0151 decision 5 allows DriverKind producers only for OwnAction and Price, so admitting synthetic Policy, Weather, Default and Supply producers amends an accepted record. WorldBranch is journalled, so adding a kind changes a journalled contract. Nothing is weakened: the change adds a typed refusal at UNDERSTAND.
decisions.adr_title: A synthetic world may declare policy, weather, default and supply drivers that no feed produces, every branch they grow stays synthetic, and no such driver reaches UNDERSTAND or REASON (amends 0151 decision 5)
decisions.closure: Add DriverKind (Policy, Weather, Default, Supply, OwnAction, Price) to qip-twin futures.rs::WorldDriver. Add a synthetic generator that, together with SyntheticMarket's participants, liquidity and structure, grows worlds along every named dimension. Test a_generator_grows_worlds_differing_along_every_named_dimension; its mutation drops one kind. Add a test that refuses a synthetic-kind driver offered to UNDERSTAND.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. futures.rs:168 WorldDriver has only id, sensitivities and evidence. grow (:382) stamps Provenance::Synthetic (:497, :707). ADR 0151 decision 5 (:77-83) gives a producer only to OwnAction and Price, so synthetic Policy, Weather, Default and Supply producers amend an accepted record, and ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT is the right route. Adding a refusal at UNDERSTAND tightens. One small misstatement: qip-contracts world_model.rs:155 WorldBranchFields (deny_unknown_fields) carries no driver, so DriverKind on qip-twin's WorldDriver does not change the journalled WorldBranch. The ADR is still needed for the 0151 amendment. The lane should know that WorldDriver is deserialized from qip-cli agency declarations (agency.rs:278). A new kind field needs explicit serde handling, not a silent default to Price.

decisions.ruling: The supply-chain twin waits on a supply-chain source licensed under ADR 0157. Port, shipping and commodity-flow data are paid subscriptions, and the choice is mine. Third-order propagation needs no vendor, so it is proved now on the causal stress. Exposure keeps its two-hop ceiling. The row stays PARTIAL until the source exists.
decisions.rationale: qip-world-model src/exposure.rs::MAX_EXPOSURE_HOPS = 2, and second_order_exposure refuses more; that ceiling is a guard and is kept. In qip-kernel src/platform.rs, CAUSAL_STRESS_MAX_ORDER = 4 is passed to reading.propagate in SIMULATE, but the only test that exercises it, tests/stress.rs::a_driver_the_understand_stage_established_from_the_tape_is_stressed_through_the_graph, walks one edge. src/now_stage.rs:29 says 'Supply chain has a domain and no feed'. qip-market-ingestion src/connectors/port_congestion.rs is 'Status: BLOCKED' on paid subscriptions, and KNOWN_SOURCES holds no supply-chain source.
decisions.closure: Now: add the qip-kernel test a_causal_stress_walks_three_established_mechanisms_and_names_the_third_order_instrument; its mutation passes order 2 to propagate. After a supply-chain source is licensed under ADR 0157: its connector, and a supply-chain twin over the entity graph.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. exposure.rs:39 sets MAX_EXPOSURE_HOPS = 2, and :153 refuses more. The ruling keeps that guard. platform.rs:1938 sets CAUSAL_STRESS_MAX_ORDER = 4, which is passed to reading.propagate at :19138. The only stress test (tests/stress.rs:694) establishes and walks the single obj-AAA -> obj-BBB edge. now_stage.rs:29 says supply chain 'has a domain and no feed'. port_congestion.rs:6 reads 'Status: BLOCKED'. decisions.ruling: A dedicated replay pool is new billed infrastructure, and decision 5 put it after the deploy. When it comes, it is a Cloud Run Job kept separate from the serving services. Its ceiling is about $105 a month, the runbook's figure for one 2 vCPU / 2 GiB instance kept warm. It sits behind a per-env switch that ships off. The row stays PARTIAL until a plan and an apply show it.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform has no google_cloud_run_v2_job, instance group or module dedicated to replay. The only Cloud Run job is google_cloud_run_v2_job.fleet in the separate infrastructure/fleet root. Hot replay indexes exist only in-process: qip-acceptance tests/tick_hot_replay_indexes.rs and qip-edge-node replay.rs. Decision 5 of owner-decisions-2026-10-25.md names 'new replay and solver pools' as declined until after the deploy. The cost comes from docs/ops/runbooks/dev-redeploy-readiness.md §5, where qip-dev-fastbrain (min 1, 2 vCPU / 2Gi) is about $105. Per-env tfvars are protected, so the switch ships as a patch. ADR 0101 C11 governs cost.
decisions.closure: After the deploy and the owner's funding: a replay-job module in infrastructure/terraform, gated by an enable_replay_pool flag that ships false. The dev tfvars line goes in a protected patch. The job has its own service account and takes no serving traffic. A tftest checks that it shares no service with serving, and a real plan is run. The row stays PARTIAL until the apply.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. Neither google_cloud_run_v2_job nor dataflow/dataproc appears under infrastructure/terraform; the only job is in infrastructure/fleet. Decision 5 declines 'new replay and solver pools' until after the deploy. The $105 is named from the runbook (dev-redeploy-readiness.md:320, qip-dev-fastbrain, min 1, 2 vCPU / 2Gi), so the cost-source rule is met. It is borrowed from a warm service and works as a one-instance-continuous ceiling for a Job. The switch ships off and nothing is applied, so the row stays PARTIAL. So it also goes in the protected patch, not only the dev tfvars line.

decisions.ruling: A physical position is a paper research record. Each unit the simulated merchant delivers becomes a RealAsset position carrying its landed cost, and its inventory state from the ledger. It stays outside the desk's book, sizing and capital, as commerce_research already promises. Any real merchant, marketplace or carrier stays refused under ADR 0021 and 0099. The commerce-only breadth plan may ship on in dev's committed configuration, because it is synthetic and fails closed.
decisions.rationale: qip-financial src/position_record.rs::PositionRecordBuilder::product_economics (LandedCost, RealAsset only) has no caller outside qip-financial. PositionRecord has no inventory-state field. qip-financial src/inventory.rs already reconciles a consignment ledger against LandedCost. The qip-kernel src/commerce_research.rs module doc says the executor holds SimulatedMerchant by concrete type and 'No commerce figure reaches the desk's sizing or capital'. That line is kept, so the scope under ADR 0021/0099 does not move. In qip-deepbrain src/breadth.rs::load, an unset plan means no breadth and an invalid plan exits 78. No env sets QIP_DEEPBRAIN_BREADTH_PLAN. The 2026-10-24 clause on default-path wiring for paper features covers switching it on.
decisions.closure: In qip-kernel commerce_research.rs, build a RealAsset PositionRecord for each received unit. Its product_economics comes from the unit's LandedCost, and a new inventory-state field is read from the Ledger. The record is held in the commerce research output and never in the book. Test a_received_paper_unit_is_a_real_asset_position_carrying_landed_cost_and_ledger_inventory_and_the_book_is_unchanged; its mutation drops the ledger read. Then mount a commerce-only breadth plan in infrastructure/gitops/envs/dev/deepbrain.yaml.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. PositionRecordBuilder::product_economics has no caller outside qip-financial, and build refuses it for anything but RealAsset (:203-207). PositionRecord is used only inside qip-financial, so adding an inventory-state field is not a cross-crate contract. commerce_research.rs:27-34 says the merchant is a SimulatedMerchant and 'No commerce figure reaches the desk's sizing or capital'. The ruling keeps that. Received units have LandedCost: commerce.rs:271, with the kernel's all_in_cost and landed.duty. breadth.rs:30 load returns None when unset, and an invalid plan exits 78. The 10-24 default-path clause covers a paper, fail-closed switch-on, and ADR 0021/0099 refusals stay. The lane must do three things. (1) manifest_wiring.rs:2240 argues QIP_DEEPBRAIN_BREADTH_PLAN unset ('a deployment sets it when the desk has written a plan, not before'), so that entry moves to the set list with the committed plan. (2) The variable names a file, so the plan must be mounted as a secret volume, the way universe.json is in deepbrain.yaml. (3) The plan may name only the synthetic commerce feed, so nothing is polled externally.

decisions.ruling: Dataflow and Dataproc stay out, because ADR 0011 keeps everything in Rust. The row is scored against its Rust equivalent, the way D4 scored the GKE rows against Cloud Run. Batch reprocessing is a Rust Cloud Run Job that reads only the archive or the warehouse and never subscribes to the live fabric. Its Terraform ships switched off. Running it is billed and comes after the deploy.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform has no google_dataflow_*, google_dataproc_* or google_cloud_run_v2_job; the only job is infrastructure/fleet's google_cloud_run_v2_job.fleet, in a separate root. ADR 0011 and .claude/rules/10-product-direction.md settle Rust everywhere, so admitting a JVM or Python engine would need an ADR, and none is warranted. owner-decisions-2026-10-11.md D4 set the precedent of scoring a refused mechanism against its Cloud Run Jobs equivalent. The requirement's verification is inspection: 'Batch jobs read GCS/BQ only; no live fabric subscription'. That can be held by a test. Replacing the requirement's named engine is a contract change, so a record comes first.
decisions.adr_title: Batch reprocessing is a Rust Cloud Run Job that reads the archive and the warehouse only and never subscribes to the fabric, and Dataflow and Dataproc stay out under 0011
decisions.closure: Three parts: a Rust reprocessing entry point that opens only the archive (qip-storage ArchiveReader) or the warehouse; a google_cloud_run_v2_job for it in infrastructure/terraform, with count gated by a flag that ships false; and the acceptance test a_batch_job_reads_only_the_archive_or_the_warehouse_and_holds_no_fabric_subscription, whose mutation adds a fabric subscribe to the job.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. infrastructure/terraform has no google_dataflow_*, google_dataproc_* or google_cloud_run_v2_job. ADR 0011's table already maps 'Dataflow — pipelines' to qip-streaming, and its Rust half stands. The requirement's verification is inspection ('Batch jobs read GCS/BQ only; no live fabric subscription'), which a test can hold. Replacing the named engine is a contract change, so ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT follows the D4 precedent and avoids the silent restatement decision 11 forbids. Shipping the Terraform off follows the repo's precedent: the Bigtable module ships with enable_bigtable=false. Two notes. The root flag goes in infrastructure/terraform/variables.tf, which is protected, so it lands as a patch the owner approves. Enabling the job is new billed spend under decision 5, so it needs its own named monthly cost. The ADR should say it reopens no spend, and the row should stay PARTIAL until a job has run.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0150 decision 5 stands. No quantum-derived feature is admitted until a family has a benefit record against a non-simulated provider. That provider, its key and its budget are billed and mine, and none is engaged now. So the ensemble-feature path is not built ahead of a benefit nobody has measured. The refusal of a quantum output offered as a model stays as it is, and the row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: qip-kernel src/model_serving.rs::promote_model_from refuses ModelProducer::QuantumGateway as a candidate (line ~1043; the row's 615-650 citation is stale) and admits QuantumInformed only with a built family and a calibrated baseline. ADR 0150 decision 5 says no binary may construct QuantumInformed until a benefit record against a non-simulated provider exists, and ComputeSettings refuses 'hosted' by name (qip-kernel src/compute_routing.rs:117). ADR 0150's BILLED list names R12-QUANT-4061. ADR 0006 requires a classical baseline. docs/blueprint/lanes/L4-quant-research-families-adr0150.patch covers the research families (QUANT-1077 and others), not this row.
decisions.closure: After a hosted provider is funded and a family commits a benefit record against it: an ensemble-feature path in qip-kernel model serving that takes a quantum output only as an input feature to an evaluated model. Its test is a_quantum_output_reaches_a_decision_only_as_a_feature_and_offering_it_as_a_model_is_refused.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. model_serving.rs:1028 promote_model_from refuses ModelProducer::QuantumGateway at :1043, and QuantumInformed at :1051 needs a baseline and a family. The row's 615-650 citation is stale, as the ruling says. compute_routing.rs:117 refuses 'hosted' by name. ADR 0150 decision 5 (:139-147) forbids any binary constructing QuantumInformed before a benefit record against a non-simulated provider exists, and :375 lists QUANT-4061 as BILLED. Guard tests serving.rs:675/715/773 exist and are kept. A paid vendor with no engagement makes this STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL.

decisions.ruling: No quantum vendor now, as with the language model in decision 6. The simulated provider stays the only one, and ComputeSettings keeps refusing hosted by name. The egress to IBM Quantum waits on an account, a key and a budget that are mine to buy. The admission half is done and stays as it is. The row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: qip-quantum src/gateway.rs::QuantumGateway::submit calls foundry::admit_job before taking a slot. qip-optimization-engine src/router.rs's QPU arm submits only through the gateway. tests/gateway.rs::an_inline_quantum_job_is_refused_and_the_provider_is_never_called holds this, and the mutation recorded in the row's notes fails it. qip-quantum src/provider.rs::HostedProvider has no production caller. qip-kernel src/compute_routing.rs:117 refuses 'hosted'. docs/ops/runbooks/dev-redeploy-readiness.md §5 records 'No QPU spend: QIP_QUANTUM_PROVIDER=simulated' and says not to seed qip-quantum-token-dev.
decisions.closure: After the owner buys an IBM Quantum account, key and per-job budget: an IBM transport behind HostedProvider, routed through the controlled egress proxy. ComputeSettings admits hosted only with that key and budget. Then its deploy. Until then nothing is built.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. gateway.rs:203 submit calls admit_job (:211) before taking a slot. The router.rs:1280 QPU arm submits only through arm.gateway.submit. tests/gateway.rs:80 an_inline_quantum_job_is_refused_and_the_provider_is_never_called exists. HostedProvider has no production caller outside qip-quantum, only doc references. compute_routing.rs:117 refuses hosted. Runbook :289 says not to seed qip-quantum-token-dev, and :331 says QIP_QUANTUM_PROVIDER=simulated. The remaining clause, egress to IBM Quantum, needs an account, a key and a budget, all paid and the owner's, and the requirement is flagged EXTERNAL_ACTION. STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL is correct, and nothing is built ahead of it.

decisions.ruling: The execution node stays off until the deploy, which comes last and is the owner's to pay for and dispatch. The code half is done, and the row closes on the plan and apply that show newyork-1 consuming its own reservation, in shadow mode.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/execution-node/main.tf::google_compute_reservation.node (count = node_count, specific_reservation_required = true) and backend/crates/tests/qip-acceptance/tests/gcp_placement.rs::every_machine_group_the_repository_defines_consumes_a_specific_reservation_sized_to_its_target already prove the constraint. infrastructure/environments/dev/terraform.tfvars::execution_nodes_enabled = false, and test/stage/prod have execution_nodes = {}, so nothing is provisioned. docs/ops/runbooks/owner-switches.md §execution_nodes_enabled sets the order: bake the image, set boot_image and region_allocation, flip the flag in a protected tfvars diff, then run infra.yml plan and up. decisions.decision: STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL with the same ruling. Correct the rationale: the test pins [COMPANY, ON_CHAIN]. Correct the closure: once a chain endpoint and its egress route exist, wire JsonRpcChainAdapter in qip-deepbrain main.rs to feed Platform::observe_chain each cycle. Test: 'a cycle with an observed chain feeds the on-chain member and ON_CHAIN is not in silent'. Do not assert that no member is silent. Mutation: drop the observe_chain call.
decisions.ruling: A member that saw nothing has produced nothing, and a silent member is reported as silent, not counted as state. Redefining the clause to pass the row is what the 2026-10-24 record rules out. Adding a synthetic chain to the default path only to make the on-chain member speak would invent blocks, so the row stays PARTIAL until a real chain node is observed through the egress proxy.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/federation_stage.rs::FederationStage::run computes silent as the population members not in `fed`. The ON_CHAIN member is fed only when FederationInputs::chain is Some. backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/tests/symbolic_federation.rs::every_cycle_journals_one_federation_review_and_each_replays_and_reproduces_its_arbitrations pins first.silent == [ON_CHAIN]. backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs::Platform::observe_chain has no non-test caller. backend/crates/services/qip-chain/src/rpc.rs::JsonRpcChainAdapter::REQUIREMENTS needs a TLS-terminating egress route and a node endpoint, and no environment commits either. Owner decision 11 forbids reading a requirement so that the row passes. The other nine members and the per-class domain members already span all five axes.
decisions.closure: Once a chain node endpoint and its egress route exist, wire JsonRpcChainAdapter in qip-deepbrain main.rs to feed Platform::observe_chain each cycle. Test: 'a cycle with an observed chain feeds the on-chain member and no member is silent'. Mutation: drop the observe_chain call.
decisions.skeptic: The outcome is right, but the rationale and closure misread the test. symbolic_federation.rs:174-177 asserts `first.silent == vec![federation_stage::COMPANY, ON_CHAIN]`, not [ON_CHAIN]. The company member (federation_stage.rs:102, R12-WORLD-3044) is also silent when no issuer surprise is sensed. So 'the other nine members' is wrong: ten other base members exist. The closure test 'a cycle with an observed chain feeds the on-chain member and no member is silent' would fail on the company member. Everything else checks out: silent = population minus fed (federation_stage.rs:1465), ON_CHAIN is fed only when inputs.chain is Some (:1335), observe_chain has only test callers, and JsonRpcChainAdapter::REQUIREMENTS exists at rpc.rs:297.
decisions.decision_detail: STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL with the same ruling. Correct the rationale: the test pins [COMPANY, ON_CHAIN]. Correct the closure: once a chain endpoint and its egress route exist, wire JsonRpcChainAdapter in qip-deepbrain main.rs to feed Platform::observe_chain each cycle. Test: 'a cycle with an observed chain feeds the on-chain member and ON_CHAIN is not in silent'. Do not assert that no member is silent. Mutation: drop the observe_chain call.

decisions.ruling: This row needs no capital. Decision 8 filed it with the live-capital rows from the triage's bucket, and I take it out. Causal drivers are measured on the graph the platform already keeps: each driver is scored by the share of the instruments its live claims reach that have history, the same way an asset class is. Language stays unmeasured, and the row stays PARTIAL on it, until a source record states the language of what it admits.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/services/qip-expansion/src/detectors.rs::CoverageDimension has only AssetClass, Venue and Geography, on purpose (ADR 0151 decision 12). The 2026-10-25 amendment to ADR 0151 showed that the causal graph is keyed on instrument ids at both ends: qip-world-model/src/causal.rs::CausalGraph::edges and ::outgoing name a cause and its effect instruments. So detectors.rs::coverage_universe can map a `causal_driver:<cause>` key to the instruments that cause's live edges reach. The existing detectors.rs::coverage then measures that key against the same history set, with no new floor and no guessed map. Language has no measured source. qip-data-finder/src/discovery_targets.rs::EntityProfile::languages is operator-stated and off by default, and no licence record carries a language.
decisions.adr_title: Causal-driver coverage is measured on the graph's own drivers against the history of the instruments they reach, and language waits for a source record that states one (amends ADR 0151 decision 12)
decisions.closure: After the ADR, add CoverageDimension::CausalDriver. Have coverage_universe (or the deep brain's map at qip-deepbrain main.rs) map each live cause in Platform::world().causal().edges() to its effect instruments. Test: 'a causal driver whose effects have no history becomes one coverage gap naming its dimension'. Mutation: drop the driver rows from the map. The row stays PARTIAL on language.
decisions.skeptic: The cited code is right. CoverageDimension has only AssetClass, Venue and Geography (detectors.rs:676). coverage() parses keys and measures them against `covered`. The ADR 0151 2026-10-25 amendment states the causal graph is keyed on instrument id at both ends. CausalGraph::edges (causal.rs:1529) and ::outgoing (:1571) exist. EntityProfile::languages is operator-stated. The refusal test uses `language:en`, so adding causal_driver weakens nothing. Taking the row out of decision 8's live-capital list opens no capital path: it is research coverage. The ADR must say that it reverses decision 8's filing as well as amending decision 12. Caveats for the lane: main.rs:234 builds the coverage map once at startup, so causal keys need a per-sweep rebuild. edges() also returns non-live edges, so filter with outgoing(cause, now).

decisions.ruling: Beliefs are probabilities, so no belief price level is built. A price/belief discrepancy is the federation's arbitrated probability landing on the wrong side of what the price then did, for the same subject, on PERSIST_SWEEPS consecutive resolutions. That raises one research item naming its origin and moves nothing. Testing it with a specialist or a simulator remains R12-EXPAND-6049's executor work.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0151 decision 12 refuses a belief price level, and that stands. backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/federation_stage.rs::Resolution already journals, per resolved instrument proposition, the federation's ensemble probability (Resolution::ensemble) and the realised outcome. That is a measured probability-space discrepancy, and nothing in it is invented. backend/crates/services/qip-expansion/src/detectors.rs::PersistenceTracker already raises exactly one Origin::PersistentDiscrepancy observation per standing run, at qip-deepbrain/src/research.rs::PERSIST_SWEEPS = 3. Today it is fed only anomaly flags (research.rs persistence.observe(&flagged)). The item is research only, so no limit or size changes.
decisions.adr_title: A price/belief discrepancy is a federation forecast the market keeps resolving against, measured in probability, and no belief price level is built (amends ADR 0151 decision 12)
decisions.closure: Add a second PersistenceTracker in research.rs. Feed it the subjects whose latest Resolution has ensemble > 0.5 with outcome false, or < 0.5 with outcome true, citing the resolved propositions. Test: 'a persistent belief discrepancy queues exactly one item naming its origin'. Mutation: feed it the anomaly flags instead.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. federation_stage.rs:229-246 Resolution has `outcome: bool` and `ensemble: Option<f64>` (R12-MODEL-6016). PersistenceTracker (detectors.rs:887) raises one Origin::PersistentDiscrepancy per run, with Wanting::Specialist. research.rs:125 has PERSIST_SWEEPS = 3. research.rs:1781 feeds it only `flagged`. Sweeps default to every cycle (every_cycles: 1), so 'consecutive sweeps' matches 'consecutive resolutions'. The item is research only, with no size or limit change, and the belief price level stays refused. It is ADR-first because it amends decision 12. The register's own closure proposed this probability-space definition, so the requirement is not being redefined to pass the row. Note for the ADR: with a near-0.5 ensemble, three straight misses happen by chance about 12% of the time, so expect noisy items.

decisions.ruling: Lead/lag is a millisecond fact between venues, and neither a bar nor a one-venue synthetic book can show one, so no residual is fed from either. The four unfed triggers wait for the tick plane under entitlements and a licensed event source. The row stays PARTIAL with its three measured triggers.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/services/qip-world-model/src/lead_lag.rs::LeadLagState::update_relationships counts a follower as a same-direction move at another venue within a 100 ms window. Bars from different venues close at the same instant, so every co-timed close would read as a zero-lag follower: an invented relationship. The synthetic exchange lists each instrument at one venue (qip-market-ingestion/src/synthetic/mod.rs, instrument.venue), so it has no cross-venue pair. ADR 0151 decision 7 leaves queue_estimate without a producer, so QueuePredictionError has no residual. WorldEventReaction needs a licensed event source (ADR 0151 decision 10). PaperReplayDivergence needs a tick replay under entitlements. qip-expansion/src/campaigns.rs::TickCampaignTrigger already accepts all four, and qip-deepbrain/src/research.rs feeds NewVenue, FillPredictionError and UnexplainedSlippage from measured fills.
decisions.closure: Once tick entitlements put a multi-venue tick tape on the tick desk, feed LeadLagState from ticks and observe AbnormalLeadLag and PaperReplayDivergence. Once a licensed event source exists, observe WorldEventReaction. Each observe call gets the test 'the trigger yields exactly one queued campaign naming its origin'.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. In lead_lag.rs:114-131, a move at or before the leader's time gets delta ZERO and counts as a follower within 100 ms, so co-timed bar closes would invent zero-lag relationships. synthetic/mod.rs:384/511 gives one venue per instrument. TickCampaignTrigger (campaigns.rs:61) has all seven triggers. research.rs:1855-1890 feeds venue, fill-prediction and slippage. Rejecting the register's 'feed LeadLagState from bars' closure is the correct, conservative call. One imprecision: QueuePredictionError's blocker is not tick entitlements. quote_loop.rs:58-70 documents that the kernel's DECIDE path never places a limit order, so QueuePosition is always Unknown. A residual needs edge-cell resting orders, which is a deployment. The row stays PARTIAL either way.

decisions.ruling: Declined for now under decision 5. The in-tree solver runs in-process within ADR 0150's bounds, and no measured queue exists to scale a pool by. A Spot job pool is reopened by an ADR that states a measured queue depth and a monthly ceiling, and only after the deploy, which is the cost taken first.
decisions.rationale: Owner decision 5 of 2026-10-25 declines new solver pools as new billed infrastructure. ADR 0150 and ADR 0190 bound solver scope to the portfolio QUBO and the in-tree constraint solver: no posed problem lies between the exact-enumeration limit (22) and the qubit ceiling (24), so the jobs are small and in-process. No Terraform module or queue exists, and the variable would sit in protected variables.tf. Neither docs/ops/runbooks/dev-redeploy-readiness.md §5 nor the row's text names a monthly cost, so FUND_THEN_DEPLOY cannot be chosen.
decisions.closure: After the deploy, an ADR states a measured solver/simulation queue depth and a monthly ceiling. Then add a Terraform job-pool module with Spot and queue-depth scaling, and a reviewed plan showing it. The row stays MISSING until then.
decisions.skeptic: This is new billed infrastructure covered by owner decision 5's decline. ADR 0190:34 confirms the window between the exact-enumeration limit of 22 and MAX_QUBITS 24 is empty, and ADR 0150 bounds solver scope. No monthly cost appears in dev-redeploy-readiness.md or in the row, so FUND_THEN_DEPLOY is correctly ruled out. Nothing is spent or implemented. The closure keeps the row MISSING.

decisions.ruling: As with the hosted language model, there is no vendor yet. An IBM Quantum account, token and QPU time are paid and the owner's, and ADR 0190 finds no posed problem that would earn hardware. The gateway's refusals stand, nothing reaches IBM, and the row stays PARTIAL until a vendor is contracted.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/libs/qip-quantum/src/gateway.rs::Delivery::Inline is always refused. backend/crates/libs/qip-quantum/tests/gateway.rs::a_job_past_its_patience_is_abandoned_keeps_its_slot_and_its_late_answer_is_discarded proves the classical fallback. backend/crates/libs/qip-quantum/src/solver.rs::IbmQuantumSolver hard-codes transport_present = false and refuses every solve. qip-quantum/src/provider.rs::HostedProvider has no caller. backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/config.rs::quantum_enabled defaults false, and the runbook records QIP_QUANTUM_PROVIDER=simulated with no QPU spend. A Qiskit Runtime client would also be a new dependency, which needs its own ADR under ADR 0109.
decisions.closure: After the owner contracts IBM Quantum and seeds qip-quantum-token-dev, and after an ADR 0109 dependency record for the client: add an async IBM adapter admitted only as a QuantumGateway entrant, retire IbmQuantumSolver's synchronous QuboSolver path, and run the timeout-yields-classical test against it.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. gateway.rs:211 refuses Delivery::Inline. solver.rs:822/837 hard-codes transport_present: false, and :860 refuses. HostedProvider appears only in doc comments and re-exports. config.rs:592 has quantum_enabled: false. The tests/gateway.rs:184 patience test exists. The runbook records QIP_QUANTUM_PROVIDER=simulated. The account and token belong to the vendor and the owner, and a Qiskit client would need an ADR 0109 record, so STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL is correct.

decisions.ruling: Declined for now under decision 5 and ADR 0191. Promoted world knowledge stays in the central brains, rebuilt from the event log, which already keeps graph load off the ledger. Spanner Graph is reopened by an ADR that states measured graph query load and a monthly ceiling, after the deploy.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0113 ('Bigtable, AlloyDB and Spanner Graph are not admitted by this record') and ADR 0191 keep the world model in-process in the central brains, versioned on the log, and not split into its own billed store before deployment. backend/crates/services/qip-world-model/src/graph.rs is the in-memory graph, and no graph query touches the ledger database, so the requirement's risk does not arise today. Then a Terraform module for a graph database separate from the ledger, an evidence-worker writer with its integration test, and a reviewed plan. The row stays MISSING until then.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. ADR 0113:57 says 'Bigtable, AlloyDB and Spanner Graph are not admitted by this record'. ADR 0191 keeps the world model in the central brains, versioned on the log. graph.rs is in-memory. Decision 5 declines new billed infrastructure, and no cost is named, so FUND_THEN_DEPLOY is correctly ruled out. Nothing is implemented.

decisions.decision: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT, capital member only. Title: 'The capital member forecasts the book's survival floor from the book's own marks and reserve, resolved by the next cycle's book, and it may only narrow (body of claimed ADR 0194)'. Closure: declare `portfolio.capital-floor.global`, feed it from positions_at_cost and the survival policy/sizing budget, and resolve it from the next cycle's book. Test: 'the capital member is in the population and produces state on a cycle with a held position'. Ruling: the federation runs every UNDERSTAND and the company member exists (R12-WORLD-3044), so 'not integrated' is stale. No counterparty member is built, because a paper book has no settlement event to resolve one. The row stays PARTIAL on the counterparty, geopolitical, supply-chain, physical and event members.
decisions.ruling: The federation runs every UNDERSTAND, so 'not integrated' is stale. Two members can be built now from the book the kernel already holds: a capital member forecasting the book's floor and a counterparty member forecasting settlement. Each has its own proposition and a resolver that reads the ledger, and each can only narrow. Geopolitical, company, supply-chain, physical and event members wait for licensed sources, and the row stays PARTIAL until they exist.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/federation_stage.rs::FederationStage declares ten members (momentum, reversion, regional microstructure, stress scenario, rare regime, alternate future, standing aside, causal graph, self, on-chain) plus domain members, covering global, regional, self, scenario and counterfactual. ADR 0151 decision 10 requires every member to have a typed proposition, a source and a resolver, and it refused a funding-draw proposition because no funding event exists. ADR 0194 is already claimed for the capital member. backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs::Platform::positions_at_cost, the survival floor of ADR 0159, and the ledger's commerce-break records of ADR 0153 are the sources and resolvers. federation_stage.rs::Narrowing has no arm above one, so a new member can only subtract from a size.
decisions.adr_title: The capital member forecasts the book's floor and the counterparty member forecasts settlement, each resolved from the ledger's own records, and neither enlarges a size (body of claimed ADR 0194)
decisions.closure: After ADR 0194's body: declare `portfolio.capital-floor.global` and `counterparty.settlement.global` in federation_stage.rs. Feed them from positions_at_cost and the survival floor, and resolve them from the ledger's floor and break records. Test: 'the capital and counterparty members are in the population and produce state on a cycle with a held position'. Macro and microstructure follow under R12-WORLD-3043 and R12-WORLD-3046.
decisions.skeptic: This rests on two misreads. (1) It says company members 'wait for licensed sources' and lists ten members without the company. But federation_stage.rs:102 declares COMPANY ('company.fundamental.global', R12-WORLD-3044), the member exists, and it is fed by fundamentals. (2) The counterparty member's resolver cites 'the ledger's commerce-break records of ADR 0153'. ADR 0153 decision 8's ReconciliationBreak is a commerce-plane break between marketplace and inventory, not trade settlement. The same decision says chargeback stays Absent because 'the plan terms carry no settlement term'. Platform::settlement_book() is a SettlementBook of jurisdiction calendars only (qip-capital-fabric settlement.rs:347), with no fail or settlement-outcome record. A paper book has no counterparty settlement event, so under ADR 0151 decision 10 the counterparty member has no resolver, exactly like the refused FundingDraw. The capital half stands: the survival policy, sizing budget and positions_at_cost exist, ADR 0194 is claimed for a capital member, and Narrowing has no arm above one.

decisions.decision: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT. Title: 'The macro member forecasts each series' next published level from the catalogued connectors, reads a surprise only where a source states consensus and labels the synthetic tape's surprises simulated, and it may only narrow (amends ADR 0151 decision 10's source clause)'. Closure: declare `macro.series-level.global` and add a macro field to FederationInputs, filled from a new now.rs reader of MACRO_LEVEL (and macro_surprises where consensus exists). Feed one proposition per series, resolved by its next reading. Test: 'a cycle with a macro reading feeds the macro member and a cycle without one reports it silent'. Update symbolic_federation.rs's silent assertion to include the macro member. The row stays PARTIAL on conflict and sanctions, and on production surprises, until a consensus-carrying licensed source exists.
decisions.ruling: Build the macro member now on the on-chain member's pattern. It reads the NOW macro partition, forecasts its own series, and is resolved by the next reading, so it speaks the day a catalogued connector is switched on at the deploy and says it is silent until then. Conflict and sanctions have no licensed source, so the row stays PARTIAL on the geopolitical half.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/services/qip-world-model/src/now.rs::macro_surprises already reads macro series from the world model, and backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs passes them to the NOW stage, but no federation member reads them. A member following federation_stage.rs's ON_CHAIN pattern (its own proposition per series, resolved by the next observed reading) meets ADR 0151 decision 10's proposition, source and resolver. FederationInputs is not journaled, so this is not a contract change. infrastructure/environments/dev/terraform.tfvars keeps deepbrain_connector (frankfurter-ecb-reference-rates) commented out until the deploy. The member is advisory and cannot enlarge a size (federation_stage.rs::Narrowing).
decisions.closure: Declare `macro.surprise-persistence.global` in federation_stage.rs. Add a macro field to FederationInputs, filled from now::macro_surprises (and macro_level for currencies). Feed one proposition per series, resolved by its next reading. Test: 'a cycle with a macro surprise feeds the macro member and a cycle without one reports it silent'.
decisions.skeptic: The core premise is false. The ruling says the member 'speaks the day a catalogued connector is switched on at the deploy'. But MacroObservation::surprise() is consensus minus value (qip-financial intelligence.rs:384), and every catalogued macro connector sets `consensus: None`: frankfurter_rates.rs:451, ecb_key_rates.rs:640 and nyfed_effr.rs:560. So now::macro_surprises stays empty in production forever, deploy or not. The only surprise producer is the synthetic adapter's scripted MacroSurprise events (synthetic/mod.rs:647-660, narrative::macro_observation with consensus Some), so on the dev path the member would be fed by simulated data with no label. Also, `macro_level` is not a function. MACRO_LEVEL is only a feature name, and now.rs has no reader for it. Building a member that is silent in every deployed environment contradicts this batch's own reasoning in 3037 and 3045. A member whose source is synthetic in dev needs the source decided by ADR, as 3046 does. So IMPLEMENT is wrong.
