decisions.ruling: Logistics, shipping and inventory vendors are billed and the owner's under ADR 0157, and none is contracted. A supply-chain member over sources nobody feeds would only add another silent member. The row stays PARTIAL until a licensed source is contracted and the weather connector is switched on at the deploy.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/services/qip-world-model/src/exposure.rs::second_order_exposure and tests/second_order.rs cover supplier relationships, but nothing models inventory, logistics or weather. ADR 0157 makes logistics, AIS, customs and IoT vendors BILLED, and vendors are the owner's. The admitted NWS weather connector is constructed only in tests, QIP_CONNECTOR_SOURCE is unset in every environment, and the egress route is not applied. Owner decision 6 sets the precedent: no vendor yet.
decisions.closure: After a licensed logistics or inventory source has a committed licence record and its egress route is applied, and the NWS connector is enabled at the deploy: add a supply-chain member in federation_stage.rs fed from those records, with a population test that it produces state.
decisions.skeptic: The outcome is correct: ADR 0157 makes logistics, AIS, customs and IoT vendors BILLED, none is contracted, and the inventory/logistics half cannot close without one. QIP_CONNECTOR_SOURCE is rendered only from deepbrain_connector, which is commented out in dev tfvars:508. One rationale misread needs fixing: 'the NWS connector is constructed only in tests' is false. qip-market-ingestion connector_feed.rs:243-246 constructs NwsStationObservationsConnector in production code (ConnectorFeed::open, used by qip-deepbrain connectors.rs). It is not enabled because no environment names it and egress is not applied. The decision does not depend on this, because its closure already says 'switched on at the deploy'.

decisions.ruling: The paper feed already states each trade's aggressor side, and like the simulated depth dataset its terms are the platform's own. So an order-flow member reads it, labelled simulated, and a licensed tape later replaces the source, not the member. A trade with no aggressor contributes nothing, and the member can only narrow a size, never enlarge one.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0151 decision 6's premise that signed order flow has no source is stale. backend/crates/services/qip-market-ingestion/src/synthetic/book.rs emits Trade { aggressor: Some(side) } on the deep brain's default synthetic adapter, and backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs's SensedRecord::Trade arm records only close and the snapshot, ignoring aggressor. ADR 0181 already treats the simulated venue's dataset as the platform's own terms. qip-data-finder's LicensingClass::Synthetic is barred from production, so in production the member falls silent until a licensed tape exists. backend/crates/services/qip-world-model/src/order_flow.rs::FlowObservation is the existing type, and federation_stage.rs::Narrowing has no arm above one (ADR 0125).
decisions.adr_title: The simulated tape's aggressor side feeds an order-flow member labelled simulated, which may only narrow, and a licensed tape replaces the source and not the member (amends ADR 0151 decision 6)
decisions.closure: After the ADR: in the platform.rs Trade arm, aggregate signed aggressor volume per instrument per cycle into FlowObservation, skipping aggressor None. Pass it through FederationInputs to a new `markets.order-flow.global.micro` member in federation_stage.rs. Test: signed_trade_flow_gives_the_order_flow_member_a_view. Mutation: ignore aggressor.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. synthetic/book.rs:202 emits `aggressor: Some(side)`. synthetic/mod.rs:400-425 generates book trades on the default synthetic environment that qip-deepbrain main.rs:593-611 builds. The platform.rs:12172 Trade arm records only close and snapshot.apply_trade (session_volume, last_trade), never signed flow. FlowObservation exists (order_flow.rs:18). ADR 0181:24/39 treats qip-simulated-depth's terms as the platform's own. reference.rs:38 bars LicensingClass::Synthetic from production, so the member falls silent there. Narrowing caps at one. ADR-first is correct because it amends ADR 0151 decision 6. No spend, no live path, and nothing loosened.

decisions.ruling: No event source is licensed, and I am not choosing one now. Vendor choice is billed and stays mine under ADR 0157, and the synthetic venue's outcome stays test-only under ADR 0151 decision 10, which ADR 0182 kept. The row stays PARTIAL until a licence record lands. Then the EventResolution proposition, its resolver and an event member are built, and not before.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/federation_stage.rs fixes its member ids as constants (MOMENTUM, REVERSION, STRESS_SCENARIO, CAUSAL_GLOBAL, RARE_REGIME, ...). None of them is an event member. qip-prediction belief.rs::Branch and resolution.rs build trees and resolve, but they feed no federation proposition. ADR 0151 decision 10 declines EventResolution until a licensed source exists. The qip-data-finder catalogue holds none (ADR 0157: a charging source needs a named owner approval). Building a member on the synthetic venue would score a random outcome as world state.
decisions.closure: Once a licence record for an event source is committed to qip-data-finder's catalogue under ADR 0157, add three things: an EventResolution proposition, a resolver that reads named observations from that source, and an event member in federation_stage.rs. Add a population check that fails when the member is absent.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. federation_stage.rs member constants are MOMENTUM (:79), STRESS_SCENARIO (:81), CAUSAL_GLOBAL (:85), RARE_REGIME (:88), COMPANY, REGIONAL_PREFIX (:109) and domain members. None is an event member. Federation propositions are string instrument propositions (instrument_proposition, :796). The kernel imports qip_prediction::resolution::Proposition only for RecordedPrediction in platform.rs:2915, not into federation. belief.rs:190 Branch exists. ADR 0151 decision 10 (:103-110) declines EventResolution until a licensed source exists and keeps the synthetic venue test-only. ADR 0182 header and decision 3 leave it standing. ADR 0157 makes vendor choice billed. No event-source licence record exists. The ruling builds nothing, eases nothing, and fails closed.

decisions.ruling: The regional member stays microstructure-only. Language, information-ecosystem and logistics inputs need licensed sources that are billed under ADR 0157, and I am not buying any before the deploy. A member widened with in-tree venue and regulation data alone would claim a scope it does not hold, so the row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: federation_stage.rs::REGIONAL_PREFIX (now at :100; the row cites :72, which is stale) builds `markets.microstructure.<region>.micro` at :955 and :1076 from tape inputs only. No catalogue entry supplies local-language news, information-ecosystem or logistics data. ADR 0157 makes the vendor choice the owner's and billed.
decisions.closure: After regional news and logistics sources are licensed: extend the regional member's inputs in federation_stage.rs to each scope axis the requirement names, with a population check per axis. Correct the REGIONAL_PREFIX citation to :100 in the meantime.
decisions.skeptic: The decision is sound. The regional member is microstructure-only and built from tape inputs. Local-language, information-ecosystem and logistics sources need ADR 0157 licences, which are billed. Declining a member partly widened from in-tree venue and regulation data is the conservative reading. The line numbers are stale on the current tree, though. Commit 9efe8b29 added the COMPANY member and shifted REGIONAL_PREFIX to :109. The rationale also says the row cites :72, but its evidence is :1 and :872. As written, the closure's 'correct to :100' would put a new wrong citation into the register. The decision does not depend on these lines.

decisions.ruling: The requirement calls quantum variants optional. ADR 0150 decision 5 keeps them unbuilt until a family has a benefit record on a non-simulated provider. The constraint is therefore the refusal at the one promotion door, and that is what this row is graded on. Land the guard test ADR 0150 promised, so that a producer cannot appear in a binary unnoticed.
decisions.rationale: model_serving.rs::Platform::promote_model_from runs two checks on its QuantumInformed arm: require_eligible_workload (Foundry::platform must hold the family Registered) and central::models::require_calibrated_baseline. Both are tested: tests/serving.rs::a_quantum_informed_candidate_is_admitted_only_with_its_calibrated_baseline_attached and ::a_quantum_informed_candidate_is_admitted_only_on_a_workload_family_the_foundry_has_built. The seam sits on the default path: qip-deepbrain/src/learning.rs:1684 calls promote_model_from (SelfFitted) in production code. The ADR-C closure test no_production_code_outside_the_promotion_seam_builds_a_quantum_informed_candidate does not exist in backend/crates/tests/qip-acceptance/tests/arch_033_quantum_path.rs, and nothing pins 'no producer' today.
decisions.closure: Add no_production_code_outside_the_promotion_seam_builds_a_quantum_informed_candidate to qip-acceptance tests/arch_033_quantum_path.rs. It scans the non-test .rs files under backend/crates and first asserts that the model_serving.rs match arm is found. It then fails on any other `ModelProducer::QuantumInformed` construction, matched as a delimited token. Mutation-check it by constructing one in qip-deepbrain main.rs. Then regrade the gap to 'none open; producer optional and unbuilt by ADR 0150 d5'.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. model_serving.rs:1051 is the QuantumInformed arm. It calls require_eligible_workload and then central::models::require_calibrated_baseline. Both tests in tests/serving.rs exist (:715 and :773). apps/qip-deepbrain/src/learning.rs:1684 calls promote_model_from(SelfFitted) in production, which corrects the row's TrainingPipeline-only claim. ADR 0150 decision 5 forbids any producer, and its Consequences say 'QUANT-4018 and QUANT-4061 share one guard test'. arch_033_quantum_path.rs does not have that test. The requirement text calls the variants optional. Adding a guard test only tightens; it needs no deployment, third party or dependency. In non-test src, `ModelProducer::QuantumInformed` appears only at :1051. The variant definition (:188) and the doc comment (:173) use the bare and Self:: forms, so the scan passes today. Suggestion: strip #[cfg(test)] modules, and also flag a `use ...ModelProducer::{..QuantumInformed..}` import or a `Self::QuantumInformed` outside the match arm, so an aliased construction cannot slip past.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0150 A2 stands, as ADR 0190 confirmed, and the parked scenario-selection family stays parked. Nothing the platform runs poses a scenario selection, so an encoding and a greedy comparison would be a benchmark for a workload nobody has. I do not reword the requirement. The row stays MISSING until there is either a benefit note or a hosted provider with a wider qubit ceiling, which is billed and mine to buy later.
decisions.rationale: qip-quantum foundry.rs::Foundry::platform registers only PortfolioAllocation and records ScenarioHypothesisSelection as NotBuilt. JobClass::HypothesisSearch has no producer. The A2 window is DEFAULT_EXACT_ENUMERATION_LIMIT 22 to statevector.rs::MAX_QUBITS 24. ADR 0190 decisions 1-2 keep docs/blueprint/lanes/L4-quant-research-families-adr0150.patch parked, so APPLY_PATCH would contradict an accepted record. decisions.decision: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT, same title. Extend the closure. (1) Add source_commit and data_manifest to ModelPack::signing_payload, and make check_releases refuse a pack missing either. The alternative is for the ADR to state the shared-key carve-out until 2027-01-31 explicitly. (3) Make qip-cli model-pack take --source-commit and --data-manifest, and write docs/blueprint/lanes/<lane>-model-pack-provenance.patch for model-pack-publish.yml. decisions.ruling: An automatic promotion moves the centre's alias and activates nothing on a cell. A model is activated only by a two-person signed ModelPack (ADR 0110): its KMS signature is the signature link, its two publishers are the approval, and the cell records commit, data manifest, signature, approvers and epoch at activation. A pack missing any link is refused, so until training carries a commit and a data manifest, no model activates.
decisions.rationale: qip-kernel model_serving.rs::ModelPromotion journals desk name and evaluation by digest. Requiring five links there would refuse every deep-brain promotion, which is lane L06's objection. qip-contracts policy.rs::ModelPack already carries the signature and publication (two people) inside its signed bytes. ModelManifest::check_releases already refuses a cell payload naming a model without a verified pack. decision_record.rs::SOURCE_COMMIT exists to stamp a commit. Adding source_commit and data_manifest to the signed bytes, and refusing a pack without them, changes a signed contract. It only adds a refusal, and no node is deployed, so it narrows nothing in use.
decisions.adr_title: A model activates on a cell only from a two-person signed pack that names its source commit and data manifest, the cell journals that activation with its epoch, and a centre promotion is not an activation

decisions.skeptic: The decision misreads the activation gate. The rationale says ModelManifest::check_releases 'already refuses a cell payload naming a model without a verified pack'. It does only under a trust bundle: qip-edge policy.rs:114-118 calls check_releases only for TrustRoot::Bundle. ADR 0110 Amendment 1 item 4 keeps shared-key cells on the pre-amendment reading until SHARED_KEY_REMOVED_AFTER = "2027-01-31" (qip-transport trust.rs:100). On a shared-key cell, a manifest-named model therefore activates with no pack. So the ruling ('a model is activated only by a two-person signed ModelPack ... a pack missing any link is refused') would be false as implemented, because the closure changes only check_releases and signing_payload. The closure also omits a second item. The pack is built by qip-cli model_pack.rs and the protected .github/workflows/model-pack-publish.yml, and both must carry the new fields through a lane patch. Without them, every published pack fails the new refusal. Failing closed there is acceptable, but the closure should say so.

decisions.decision: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT. Title: 'A compiled plan, with any model it carries inline, reaches an execution node baked into its attested image beside the trust bundle; the signed payload names the plan's digest and a two-person pack names each model's; a node fetches neither at run time'. Closure: (1) write the ADR; (2) have provision.sh install committed plan files to a fixed /etc/qip/plans/ directory, the way it installs trust files; (3) write the image.yml staging change as a docs/blueprint/lanes/*.patch; (4) leave strategy_plan_path in tfvars as the owner's switch; (5) cite the existing tests/strategies.rs:383 as evidence instead of adding a test. The row stays PARTIAL until a node is deployed.
decisions.ruling: No bucket or registry is bought to carry plans to nodes. A model reaches a node only inline in its two-person signed pack inside the policy payload. A compiled plan reaches it baked into the attested node image, beside the trust bundle, and nothing is fetched at run time. The cell admits either only at the digest the signed payload names, and the row stays PARTIAL until a node is deployed.
decisions.rationale: qip-contracts policy.rs::PlanDigest says 'the plan itself ships elsewhere'. qip-edge-node strategies.rs::PLAN_VARIABLE (QIP_STRATEGY_PLAN_PATH) reads a local file capped at MAX_PLAN_BYTES, and nothing writes that file. ModelPack::inline_model plus ModelManifest::check_releases already deliver models over the mesh. ADR 0110 bakes the trust bundle into the attested image and rejects fetching it at run time; applying the same reasoning to plans avoids a paid store. execution_nodes_enabled = false in dev, so deployment evidence waits on the owner.
decisions.adr_title: A compiled plan reaches an execution node baked into its attested image, a model rides inline in its signed pack, and a node fetches neither at run time
decisions.closure: Write the ADR. Then have modules/image-bake place the compiled plan at a fixed path that modules/execution-node passes as strategy_plan_path. Add a qip-edge-node test that a baked plan whose digest the signed payload does not name is refused. Deployment evidence follows the owner's node switch.
decisions.skeptic: The decision rests on a misread. The ruling and rationale say a model reaches a node 'inline in its two-person signed pack' and that 'ModelPack::inline_model plus ModelManifest::check_releases already deliver models over the mesh'. They do not. InlineModel (policy.rs) is only {name, digest}, and the ModelManifest doc says 'Weights never travel this fabric'. Model weights ride inside the compiled plan: qip-strategy ir.rs:250 Expr::Model carries a DistilledModel. So baking the plan bakes the model, and the pack and manifest only authorise its digest. The closure also names the wrong module. modules/image-bake is the bake's bucket, builder identity and subnet (main.tf:1-20). Image content is infrastructure/images/execution-node/provision.sh, which installs trust files at /etc/qip/trust (:194-197), and it is staged by .github/workflows/image.yml, a protected path. Finally, the test the closure wants to add already exists: qip-edge-node tests/strategies.rs:383 a_plan_whose_bytes_are_not_the_ones_the_payload_names_deploys_nothing.

decisions.ruling: Rollback is to a model artefact, which is what the row's own check names, and it is built: a drifted model is retired and its predecessor returns at the digest that passed. A retired strategy is never rolled back; it comes back only as a new candidate up the whole promotion ladder, so retirement stays terminal and the one path to capital keeps its one entrance.
decisions.rationale: Requirement (docs/blueprint/requirements/R12-M6.json, MODEL domain) checks 'a degraded model's predecessor returns at the digest that passed; a rollback with no known-good predecessor is refused'. Met: qip-kernel/src/model_serving.rs::Platform::rollback_model reads the predecessor from the log at its first-promoted digest and refuses when none verifies; reached on the deep brain default path via qip-deepbrain/src/evolution.rs:726 -> learning.rs::LearningDesk::roll_back_degraded; tests qip-kernel/tests/serving.rs::a_degraded_model_is_retired_and_the_one_it_displaced_returns_at_the_digest_that_passed, ::a_rollback_refuses_a_predecessor_whose_card_no_longer_carries_the_digest_that_passed, ::a_rollback_with_no_known_good_predecessor_is_refused_and_changes_nothing. The strategy reading came from a grader's gap, not the requirement; qip-lifecycle/src/ledger.rs::record_promotion refuses a retired strategy ('re-proposed as a new candidate under a new identity') and tests/lifecycle.rs::retirement_is_terminal_and_a_retired_strategy_must_be_re_proposed_as_a_new_candidate pins it. decisions.ruling: Every formed hypothesis already passes the rule pack before approval, whoever proposed it, so the invariant holds for any proposer. No neural model proposes anything here, and a ridge card is not relabelled neural, nor is a model proposer added to the decision path just to exercise the veto. The neural half waits on a contracted hosted model (decision 6), and when one exists its output enters only as a hypothesis the rule pack can veto.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0145 stands: the one act this platform takes is an internal draft, its effect is filed as measured and unidentified, and nobody calls it causal. Learning a causal effect needs an action in the world or a hold-out on the desk, and neither is opened, so the row stays PARTIAL on that clause. This is a refusal of an external action surface and is said so.
decisions.rationale: The flow goal -> levers -> candidates -> simulate -> gate -> act -> attribute runs in qip-cli/src/agency.rs (engine::run with the Unwired adapter, then engine::learn_shadowed, journaled AgencyRecord::Learned), and on the deep brain in qip-deepbrain/src/ambient_agency.rs::AmbientAgency::learn_stages (engine::learn, Identification::NotIdentified at identifiability 0). The unmet clause is 'learns their measured causal effect': ADR 0145 decisions 1 and 3 forbid describing the effect as causal and assigning any treatment, and decision 8 revives an identified estimator only with an ADR amending 0114 D8 plus a consumer under ADR 0141. The row is flagged EXTERNAL_ACTION.

The shadow binary already accepts an operator-run, binary-drawn hold-out (Experiment::design, COVERAGE-7188, test agency.rs:520), but uses it only to widen a shadow policy, not to learn an effect. decisions.ruling: The Curiosity Engine of §9.10 is the acquisition rank: AcquisitionCriteria::net_value_bp, ordered by rank_acquisitions. The expansion curriculum keeps its EXPAND-6063 order, because an unhurried, valuable question is still worth asking. Cost enters as (1 − cost), the share of the decision's value the evidence leaves, since a rank that rose with price would buy expensive evidence. A gap's severity stands for its uncertainty until an observation states a measured reduction of its own.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/libs/qip-contracts/src/ambient.rs::AcquisitionCriteria::net_value_bp computes significance × uncertainty × urgency × (MAX − cost) in integer arithmetic. rank_acquisitions drops zero ranks. backend/crates/apps/qip-deepbrain/src/research.rs::cheapest_viable and admit (urgency_bp from the deadline) feed it. Both tests were mutation-verified on 2026-10-24. services/qip-expansion/src/curriculum.rs::Criteria::score (lines 153-167) already documents that urgency boosts there and gates only in the Curiosity Engine. Changing it would reopen R12-EXPAND-6063, a COMPLETE row, and loosen its tested zero-urgency rule. The narrowing and the (1 − cost) form are recorded in no ADR, and the row's gap asks for one.
decisions.closure: Write the ADR. Restate the row to the acquisition rank, recording the (1 − cost) form and severity-as-uncertainty, with spread on the federation path. Grade it on a_deferred_gap_admitted_beside_a_fresh_one_ranks_first_through_admit and the_curiosity_rank_is_monotone_in_every_factor_and_zero_when_any_factor_is. Make no code change, and leave curriculum.rs untouched.

decisions.ruling: A specialist model is trained only from a source a licence record admits. Volatility and regime qualify now, from the licensed bars. Event probability, valuation, liquidity, default, demand and supply wait on licence records under ADR 0157. A paper fill trains no slippage model, because it would learn our own fill simulator and call that the market. Each trained class is read by one named warm-lane consumer that may only narrow and refuses when its model is absent. A specialist is refused at hot-lane admission.

The deep brain trains only next-bar return regressors (qip_training::local). libs/qip-numerics/src/hmm.rs and the bar history support regime and volatility fits; the other six need sources that ADR 0157 says enter only by licence record, and vendors are the owner's. ADR 0155 ('a belief never enlarges a size') and ADR 0151 (an outside prior may only narrow) set the narrowing-only consumer. Naming a consumer per class is a contract change.

decisions.ruling: An ambient model reaches a fast lane only as the signed distillate of a fitted teacher with its own training rows and holdout. The now-stage filter is not a teacher, and a student fitted to its own outputs is refused as the filter relabelled. Until such a teacher exists and R12-CONTRACT-7064's release path can name a pack to a cell, no ambient model reaches a fast lane in any form. The row stays PARTIAL on its positive half.
decisions.rationale: The NOW stage's expected-state estimator is a local-level filter. Its surprises reach attention through the deep brain's now.rs surprise_signals, with test tests/qip-acceptance/tests/ambient_attention.rs. backend/crates/services/qip-training/src/distill.rs::distil needs a fitted teacher with training rows, and none exists for the filter. The prohibition half is already pinned transitively by tests/qip-acceptance/tests/arch_001_independent_reflex.rs::nothing_the_edge_node_links_directly_or_transitively_is_a_cognitive_crate, whose COGNITIVE list includes qip-world-model and qip-training. decisions.closure: Write the ADR. Restate the gap to name the two prerequisites: a fitted surprise teacher with training rows, and R12-CONTRACT-7064. Keep arch_001_independent_reflex as the prohibition's pin. No student is fitted to the filter's outputs, so there is no code change now.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0149 decision 13 stands: the influence weights and the compute allocation stay journaled records that govern nothing. Build the measurement d13 names now. Only when the influence-weighted aggregate beats the equal-weight mean on resolved questions out of sample does an amendment let the allocation narrow the deep brain's fit budget, never widen it.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/services/qip-learning-engine/src/tournament.rs::Tournament::compute_allocation (line 1505) is computed once per regime at runtime/qip-kernel/src/model_tournament.rs:1075 and journaled. The module doc's 'Advisory' section (model_tournament.rs:52-60) says the weights and allocation are records. ADR 0149 d13 conditions any narrowing use on an out-of-sample win of the weighted over the unweighted aggregate. Nothing computes that comparison today: tournament.rs:1946 an_earned_aggregate_is_not_the_equal_weight_mean_of_its_forecasts only asserts that the two differ. Without the measurement the condition can never be met.
decisions.closure: Each LEARN, journal beside the TournamentReview the out-of-sample Brier score of the influence-weighted aggregate and of the equal-weight mean. Score only questions resolved after the weights were fixed. The record gates nothing. Test: a_measurement_is_journaled_and_reads_nothing_back. Mutation: score both aggregates with the same weights.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. Tournament::compute_allocation is at tournament.rs:1505. The kernel calls it at model_tournament.rs:1075 and journals the result. No such comparison exists: tournament.rs:1946 only asserts that the two differ, and grep finds no out-of-sample or equal-weight scorer. Building a journaled measurement that gates nothing adds evidence and loosens nothing. It needs no deployment or third party, so IMPLEMENT is right, and the allocation stays advisory.

decisions.ruling: The population is the learning desk's own fitted models. Each decision-eligible card forecasts only its own instrument's question, on the deep brain's existing capacity at no new spend, and a drifted card leaves. No per-regime clones and no forecasts from branches no model answers: 'thousands' is a scale the real models reach, never a count padded to, and the row stays PARTIAL until they reach it.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0149 decision 12 says an entrant is a function that exists, and a population of thousands is not a goal. qip-world-model/src/spawning.rs::WorldModelSpawner has no residual producer: qip-kernel/src/attribution.rs closes P&L exactly, so nothing is left unexplained. The live entrants are only detector:<class> and analyst:<agent>, per runtime/qip-kernel/src/model_tournament.rs::model_vote and the stage around line 412. qip-deepbrain/src/learning.rs::LearningDesk fits, registers and drift-scores per-instrument ModelCards (qip-ai/src/registry.rs::ModelCard) that are real forecasting functions. qip-learning-engine/src/tournament.rs holds MAX_FORECASTERS=4096. Admitting a new entrant id form and turning a return fit into a directional probability changes the ADR 0149 section C forecaster contract, so an ADR comes first. The tournament stays advisory (ADR 0125; ADR 0149 decision 13).
decisions.adr_title: A fitted model card is a tournament entrant only on its own instrument's question, its probability comes from its own holdout error, and the population is never padded to a count
decisions.closure: Admit each decision-eligible LearningDesk card as a `model:<card id>` Specialist on tournament questions whose subject is the card's instrument. Take P(up) from the fit's own holdout residual error and drop the entrant when ModelCard::decision_eligibility refuses. Test: a_drifted_card_casts_no_forecast_and_an_eligible_one_is_scored.

LearningDesk is at learning.rs:773 and ModelCard::decision_eligibility at registry.rs:657. MAX_FORECASTERS = 4_096 and ForecasterKind::Specialist exist. model_tournament.rs:921 already names a `model:<reference>` record in verify_model, but nothing admits that form. The tournament stays advisory (ADR 0149 decision 13, ADR 0125), so new entrants move no decision. The ruling keeps 'thousands' as the bar and does not redefine it.

decisions.decision: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT. Title: 'A reflex package is drafted unsigned by the deep brain and signed only by the two-person model-pack publish, and no running process holds a package signer' (amends ADR 0131 decision 1 and its Consequences). Once the ADR is accepted, build the closure as written: unsigned drafts under REFLEX_PACKAGES_NAMESPACE, `qip reflex-package signing-message|attach-signature` verbs, the LocalSigner test under QIP_DEPLOYMENT=local, and the refusal test. The row stays PARTIAL until the protected model-pack-publish.yml signing step and the key version exist.
decisions.ruling: No running process signs a reflex package. The deep brain writes each package as an unsigned draft, and the two-person model-pack publish signs it, exactly as a model pack, so the deep brain never holds the model-pack key; until that publish step exists, held_unsigned stays the honest count.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0131 decision 1 says reflex packages sign under model-pack, two-person, and 'the deep brain never holds cloudkms.signer alone'. qip-api/src/signing.rs::SIGNED_HERE says 'Model packs are signed by the publish workflow, never by a running process'. qip-cli/src/model_pack.rs::signing_message_hex and ::attach_signature are the publish verbs model-pack-publish.yml drives. qip-contracts/src/reflex_package.rs::PackageSigner and SignedReflexPackage::sign already refuse a blank signature. qip-deepbrain/src/main.rs, around lines 899-937, installs no signer and writes held packages nowhere. No lane patch exists under docs/blueprint/lanes for the workflow half, so APPLY_PATCH does not apply. The code half fits ADR 0131 and ADR 0149 and adds a refusal without lifting one.
decisions.closure: Have ResearchLoop write held packages as unsigned drafts under REFLEX_PACKAGES_NAMESPACE and add `qip reflex-package signing-message|attach-signature` verbs mirroring model_pack.rs. Run research_market.rs's published-package test with LocalSigner under QIP_DEPLOYMENT=local, and add a test that a deployed deep brain refuses a configured package signer. The row stays PARTIAL until a protected patch adds the signing step to model-pack-publish.yml and the model-pack key version exists.
decisions.skeptic: The ruling contradicts an accepted ADR while claiming it 'fits ADR 0131'. ADR 0131 decision 1 says: 'The deep brain's PackageSigner is the KMS signer under the model-pack key'. Its Consequences name 'the KMS PackageSigner installed in qip-deepbrain/src/main.rs' as the code slice for REASON-7203. ADR 0149 'Not decided here' (line 568) repeats this: 'installing a KMS-backed PackageSigner in the deep brain'. The ruling says the opposite: no running process signs, and the closure adds a test that 'a deployed deep brain refuses a configured package signer'. That is an architecture change that needs an ADR first. The direction itself is sound and tighter. It mirrors ADR 0149 decision 3, where the deep brain drafts the model pack unsigned and the workflow signs it, and it matches qip-api signing.rs::SIGNED_HERE ('Model packs are signed by the publish workflow, never by a running process'). The other citations check out: REFLEX_PACKAGES_NAMESPACE exists (qip-storage classes.rs:34, already wired via with_package_store in main.rs:924). model_pack.rs::signing_message_hex and ::attach_signature exist. The blank-signature refusal is at reflex_package.rs:231. No lane patch exists.

decisions.decision: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT, same title. The ruling must drop 'the promotion gate's calibration floor'. The ADR must name the exact existing constant each HealthRequirement field comes from: max_staleness from CellConfig::max_staleness, and model max_staleness from ModelCard.evaluation_validity. Where no existing number fits min_quality_bp, the ADR must argue the value as its own record, not borrow one silently. The rest of the closure stands: map LimitSet hard limits, MaxDrawdown per standard_library scenario and a stated EmergencyMode; produce no envelope without MaxDrawdown; strict cell decode refusing any missing slot; and the named test.
decisions.ruling: The cell gets the typed envelope, built only from numbers that already exist. Hard limits come from the limit set as it stands. Each standard stress scenario is bounded at the limit set's MaxDrawdown. The health requirements are the slot staleness bounds the cell already enforces and the promotion gate's calibration floor, and the emergency mode is stated, never assumed. A limit set with no drawdown limit produces no envelope, and a cell refuses a payload with any slot missing and takes no new exposure on it.
decisions.rationale: qip-contracts/src/risk_envelope.rs::RiskEnvelopeFields requires at least one scenario limit and one health requirement. qip-risk/src/limits.rs::LimitKind has neither a scenario-loss kind nor a health threshold. qip-api/src/mesh.rs (around line 941) ships only RiskEnvelopeSnapshot { limits: Value }. qip-kernel/src/platform.rs::STRESS_LOSS_TOLERANCE is documented as 'not a limit', so I do not convert it. MaxDrawdown is an existing limit, so reusing it invents no number (2026-10-24 'no change to a financial risk limit'; decision 7). risk_envelope.rs itself says moving the payload onto this type 'is a change to the policy frame and the risk engine together', so it is a contract change and needs an ADR. Every added check is a refusal, which tightens.
decisions.adr_title: The policy payload's risk envelope is the typed RiskEnvelope, built only from limits that already exist, and a cell refuses one with a slot missing
decisions.closure: Replace RiskEnvelopeSnapshot in PolicyPayload.risk_envelope with RiskEnvelope. Map LimitSet hard limits, MaxDrawdown per standard-library scenario, the cell's slot staleness bounds and the promotion calibration floor in qip-api mesh.rs, and decode it strictly in the cell. Test: a_policy_payload_whose_risk_envelope_lacks_a_scenario_limit_is_refused_by_the_cell. Close R12-CONTRACT-1195 with the same change.
decisions.skeptic: Most citations check out. RiskEnvelopeFields has hard_limits, scenario_limits, driver_limits, health_requirements and emergency_mode. LimitKind has MaxDrawdown (limits.rs:186) but no scenario kind. mesh.rs:941 ships RiskEnvelopeSnapshot { limits }. platform.rs:1925 documents STRESS_LOSS_TOLERANCE as 'not a limit'. risk_envelope.rs says the move 'is a change to the policy frame and the risk engine together'. ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT is the right kind. But the ruling rests on 'built only from numbers that already exist', and one of its sources does not exist: 'the promotion gate's calibration floor'. HealthRequirement.min_quality_bp needs a value. PromotionBar (qip-learning-engine feedback.rs:107) holds only minimum_support, minimum_smoothed_support and minimum_distinct_contributors, with no calibration term. qip-ai registry.rs has no calibration gate. confidence.rs::CALIBRATION_FLOOR (0.25) is a sizing-multiplier floor, and lattice_stage.rs::CALIBRATION_BRIER_BOUND (0.30) is an SLO, not a promotion gate. A lane following the closure would have to invent or repurpose a quality threshold. That is what the row's own reason warned about ('a producer written now would invent risk limits'), and 2026-10-25 decision 7 requires such a number to be argued in its own record.

decisions.decision: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT. The ADR must do four things. (a) Carry the delta to the centre as a lib-level record on a named transport, not as the app type AmbientRecord. If the deployed transport needs an undeployed fabric, the deployed half is STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY. (b) Count a delta only if its window_end is after the hold's raised_at and its model_version matches the venue's current calibration. (c) State the residual criterion as a new tightening argued in the ADR, not as 'existing values'. (d) Apply it per strategy held at the venue. Same test name and the same drop-the-receive mutation.
decisions.ruling: The receiver is the central brain's divergence hold. A re-promotion releases a venue's hold only when the latest MicrostructureDelta concluded for that venue sits inside the thresholds I approved in decision 2. A residual may keep a hold. It never lifts one, and it never sizes anything.
decisions.rationale: The gap is stale. backend/crates/apps/qip-deepbrain/src/research.rs::ResearchLoop::conclude_campaigns builds the delta through backend/crates/services/qip-expansion/src/campaigns.rs::TickCampaignDetector::conclude on the default sweep. It journals the delta as backend/crates/apps/qip-deepbrain/src/ambient_journal.rs::AmbientRecord::MicrostructureDelta under cell "qip-deepbrain", and no other brain reads it. The delta's model_version is the twin's fill calibration ("twin-fill-calibration/{venue}@{n}"). The decision that calibration already argues is backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/replay_divergence.rs (REPLAY_DIVERGENCE_THRESHOLD_BPS=100, REPLAY_DIVERGENCE_MIN_SAMPLE=10, values approved in decision 2). Making the delta a condition on releasing a hold adds a refusal. It uses existing values and no new limit. ADR 0133, 0151 and 0152 require a named consumer, and this is a cross-app seam (deepbrain journal to qip-api's Platform), so it needs an ADR.
decisions.adr_title: A concluded microstructure delta is read by the centre's divergence hold; a residual may keep a venue's hold but never lift one or size anything
decisions.closure: qip-api's central plane reads AmbientRecord::MicrostructureDelta from the ambient journal, re-admits each through MicrostructureDelta::new, and replay_divergence refuses to release a venue's hold while that venue's latest delta's |observed - modelled| exceeds REPLAY_DIVERGENCE_THRESHOLD_BPS on at least REPLAY_DIVERGENCE_MIN_SAMPLE samples; this is proven by a_concluded_tick_campaigns_delta_keeps_the_venues_divergence_hold (mutation: drop the receive call and the hold releases), and the row's stale gap is rewritten to name the producer.
decisions.skeptic: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT is the right bucket, but the ruling misreads the code in four places. (1) It claims the change 'uses existing values and no new limit'. That is wrong. replay_divergence.rs::measure applies REPLAY_DIVERGENCE_THRESHOLD_BPS to the mean ABSOLUTE trade error over at least 10 fills. research.rs::conclude_campaigns sets observed = the mean SIGNED trade_error_bps and modelled = calibration.bias_bps, over at least MIN_REMEASURED = 5 fills per instrument. |observed - modelled| is a different statistic, so putting 100 bps on it is a new criterion that borrows a number. (2) The closure has qip-api decode AmbientRecord::MicrostructureDelta. AmbientRecord is defined in apps/qip-deepbrain/src/ambient_journal.rs, and 00-boundaries.md says 'nothing may depend on an app'. That journal is also the deep brain's own file (QIP_DEEPBRAIN_AMBIENT_JOURNAL, 'Its own log, not the platform's ... Nothing here reads the log back into a decision'). qip-api has no read path to it, so on a deployed qip-api the condition could never fire. (3) Holds are keyed per strategy (platform.rs replay_divergence_holds: BTreeMap<StrategyId, DivergenceHold>), not per venue. (4) Using 'the latest delta' with no window or model_version check can hold a strategy forever on a delta from before recalibration. That contradicts the module's own rule that the evidence window restarts at the re-promotion.

(b) Count a delta only if its window_end is after the hold's raised_at and its model_version matches the venue's current calibration. (c) State the residual criterion as a new tightening argued in the ADR, not as 'existing values'. (d) Apply it per strategy held at the venue. Same test name and the same drop-the-receive mutation.

decisions.ruling: The receiver is the deep brain's gap detector. If a partition's WorldModelState passes its expiry with no successor, the deep brain raises a model-drift gap and queues re-estimation. The state never moves a size and never chooses an action.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/now_stage.rs::NowStage::run pushes NowReview.world_states on world_model.updated, and nothing reads them back. ADR 0151 decision 4 withholds a brain receiver until a brain names a decision the state feeds, and bar part 4 keeps the text 'between brains'. The deep brain already decodes that topic: backend/crates/apps/qip-deepbrain/src/research.rs counts knowledge_deltas (R12-EXPAND-6039). backend/crates/services/qip-expansion/src/gap.rs::GapTrigger::ModelDrift is an existing research trigger. backend/crates/libs/qip-contracts/src/world_model.rs::WorldModelStateFields::expires_at gives a deterministic condition. The receiver only queues research, so it adds nothing that sizes or acts. It amends ADR 0151 decision 4, so it needs an ADR.
decisions.adr_title: WorldModelState's receiver is the deep brain's gap detector: an expired partition queues re-estimation and moves no size
decisions.closure: The deep brain's sweep reads NowReview.world_states from world_model.updated, re-admits each through WorldModelState::new, and raises a GapTrigger::ModelDrift observation for any partition past expires_at with no newer state; this is proven by a_partition_whose_world_state_expired_queues_a_model_drift_gap (mutation: drop the read and no gap is raised).
decisions.skeptic: Verified. now_stage.rs::NowStage::run pushes world_states, but only for partitions this pass moved. research.rs reads platform.knowledge_deltas() from Topic::WorldModelUpdated. gap.rs::GapTrigger::ModelDrift exists and research.rs already handles it. world_model.rs::WorldModelStateFields::expires_at exists. ADR 0151's 'What would make this wrong' already says decision 4 is superseded 'for that brain only' once a brain names a decision, so an ADR amendment is the right path. The receiver only queues research within the sweep's existing acquisition budget, so it sizes nothing and loosens nothing. One point the lane should know: states are journalled only on a move, so 'no successor past expires_at' is exactly the stale-partition signal.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0119 already answers placement. The mirror is an asynchronous consumer in the target region, deployed only at a second region, and ADR 0035 still runs one region. The replicated journal is the Spanner managed log, which decision 5 keeps unbought. I set no cost ceiling for something I am not buying, and the row stays PARTIAL until both exist in a deployment.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/libs/qip-events/src/event_fabric/policy.rs::StreamPolicy::new refuses replication_factor != 1 (C2) and any Mirroring but None (C8). ADR 0119 decisions 1-3 (accepted) fix the mirror's shape and placement and defer its deployment to a second region, which needs a record superseding ADR 0035. Replication exists only as the paid Spanner managed log behind QIP_EVENT_FABRIC_MANAGED_LOG=spanner, on a fabricd that ADR 0010 keeps undeployed. docs/ops/runbooks/dev-redeploy-readiness.md gives no monthly cost for either, so FUND_THEN_DEPLOY is not available. Building the mirror's policy arm would lift a StreamPolicy refusal, so it is not done under this row; it belongs to R12-FABRIC-7038 under ADR 0119. This composite (§31 checklist) closes only when every constituent is deployed.
decisions.closure: No code under this row. It stays PARTIAL until the owner funds the Spanner managed log with a stated monthly ceiling and a second-region record supersedes ADR 0035; the mirror itself is built under R12-FABRIC-7038 per ADR 0119.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. policy.rs refuses mirroring != None with 'BLOCKED(C8): fabric-mirror is not built'. ADR 0119 decision 1 fixes the mirror's shape (async, in the target region). Decision 3 builds it now and defers deployment to a second region, which needs a record superseding ADR 0035. The Spanner managed log falls under owner decision 5 (declined), and no monthly cost is named, so FUND_THEN_DEPLOY is unavailable. Lifting the policy arm stays with R12-FABRIC-7038. A minor imprecision: StreamPolicy also admits MANAGED_REPLICATION_FACTOR for P0/P1 (ADR 0111 §3), so 'refuses != 1' is approximate. The bucket does not depend on it.

decisions.ruling: Discovery proposes and the operator permits. The signed policy carries an operator-signed market reference, and the cell reports any cycle it finds outside the whitelist and sends nothing on it. Only the whitelist reaches the send path. The distributed half waits on a second node, which decision 5 keeps unbought.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0154 decision 1 refused discovery because 'discovery adds conversions nobody signed'. A cycle that is reported and never sent adds no conversion to what trades, and the operator signs the reference. ADR 0154 asked for exactly that answer to 'who signs discovery'. The requirement's own check is 'a discovered cycle outside the whitelist is reported', not traded. Today backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/arbitrage.rs::registry_from_books and Installation::InstalledWithGaps already report unwhitelisted book sides without adding edges (MESH-023), but they cannot form a cycle because a book carries no from/to (backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/central/whitelist.rs::ArbitragePolicy::whitelist_for is the only source of conversions). Adding a market reference to the signed payload is a contract change, so it needs an ADR. Distributed scanning needs a peer node; docs/blueprint/lanes/l5b-peer-mesh-root.patch notes a second node is billed and declined.
decisions.adr_title: Discovery proposes and the operator permits: a cycle outside the whitelist is reported and never sent, the centre's whitelist is the operator's markets narrowed to the cycles it discovers, and an inventory target may only be lowered
decisions.closure: Add an operator-signed market reference (market to base/quote per venue) to the policy payload. The cell searches every held book over it and journals each cycle with an edge outside the whitelist as a discovered-cycle record, sending no order; this is proven by a_discovered_cycle_outside_the_whitelist_is_reported_and_never_sent (mutation: route it to the send path and the test fails).
decisions.skeptic: Verified. arbitrage.rs::registry_from_books and Installation::InstalledWithGaps exist. whitelist_for builds conversions only from the operator's ArbitragePolicy markets. ADR 0154 'What would make this wrong' invites a record saying who signs discovery. l5b-peer-mesh-root.patch records that a second node is billed and declined by decision 5. Adding a market reference to the signed payload is a contract change, so it needs the ADR. Reporting cycles while sending none adds no conversion to what trades. One fix is required: the shared ADR title's last clause, 'an inventory target may only be lowered', is a misread (see R12-MESH-5059) and must be replaced in the ADR this row shares.

decisions.decision: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT, with a corrected shared title: 'Discovery proposes and the operator permits: a cycle outside the whitelist is reported and never sent, the centre's whitelist is the operator's markets narrowed to the cycles it discovers, and inventory targets stay the operator's numbers'. Closure: the centre enumerates templates over the operator's ArbitragePolicy markets, ships only the conversions on a template (journalled on WhitelistIssue), and keeps inventory_targets as the operator-stated values. The only change allowed is omitting a target for an instrument on no template; the cell already refuses to mirror an instrument with no target. Proven by the_centre_publishes_a_whitelist_from_discovery_and_stopping_discovery_empties_it. The row stays PARTIAL on prepositioning beyond the operator's numbers (owner decision 7).
decisions.ruling: The centre discovers templates only inside what the operator signed. Slot 8 carries the operator's conversions narrowed to the cycles the centre finds over them, so stopping discovery empties it. Candidates that cells report wait for my operator's signature. Inventory targets stay the operator's numbers, which a template may only lower, so nothing new is sized, as decision 7 requires.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/central/whitelist.rs::ArbitragePolicy::whitelist_for ships every signed conversion and leaves cycles empty ('the centre enumerates no cycles'). backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/central/plane.rs's issue path already narrows by omission only (withdrawn venues, ADR 0154 decision 3's min fill bound). Enumerating templates over the signed graph, and shipping only the conversions on a template, is discovery that can only shrink the permission. It also meets the requirement's mutation: stop discovery and the whitelist is empty. Inventory targets ride PolicyPayload::inventory_targets (backend/crates/libs/qip-contracts/src/policy.rs). Lowering them only keeps ADR 0154 decision 1's operator-stated ceiling and decision 7's 'nothing new is sized', reserved as ADR 0154 decision 8's DirectionalBand against the share. This revisits ADR 0154 decision 1, so it shares the 5042 ADR.
decisions.adr_title: Discovery proposes and the operator permits: a cycle outside the whitelist is reported and never sent, the centre's whitelist is the operator's markets narrowed to the cycles it discovers, and an inventory target may only be lowered
decisions.closure: The centre enumerates cycle templates over the operator's signed markets at each issue, ships only conversions on a template (journalled on WhitelistIssue), and produces inventory_targets as the lower of the operator-stated target and each template's start size; this is proven by the_centre_publishes_a_whitelist_from_discovery_and_stopping_discovery_empties_it.
decisions.skeptic: Narrowing the whitelist to conversions on centre-discovered templates is a real narrowing. whitelist_for ships every signed conversion, and unwind_plan only trades books already filled, so no unwind route is lost. The inventory half, however, misreads the code. An inventory target is not a ceiling. Cell (cell.rs ~8766) centres §31.1's two-sided band on it via discipline.band_around(target). qip-routing mirror.rs::InventoryBand::posture then sets the permitted direction and size from the holding's deviation from that target. Lowering a target can move a holding from BelowTarget (BuyOnly) to AtTargetInsideBand (Either), which opens Sell. It can also move a holding from AtTarget (Reduced) to AboveTarget or OutsideHardBand (SellOnly, Full), which lifts the size discipline. That loosens a gate. Also, 'the lower of the target and each template's start size' compares a trade size (start_sizes, including the envelope's order_limit) with a holding. The units differ. Finally, ADR 0154 decision 8's DirectionalBand does not exist in code (grep finds none), so 'reserved as DirectionalBand' describes nothing built.
decisions.decision_detail: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT, with a corrected shared title: 'Discovery proposes and the operator permits: a cycle outside the whitelist is reported and never sent, the centre's whitelist is the operator's markets narrowed to the cycles it discovers, and inventory targets stay the operator's numbers'. Closure: the centre enumerates templates over the operator's ArbitragePolicy markets, ships only the conversions on a template (journalled on WhitelistIssue), and keeps inventory_targets as the operator-stated values. The only change allowed is omitting a target for an instrument on no template; the cell already refuses to mirror an instrument with no target. Proven by the_centre_publishes_a_whitelist_from_discovery_and_stopping_discovery_empties_it. The row stays PARTIAL on prepositioning beyond the operator's numbers (owner decision 7).

decisions.ruling: Legs stay risk-ordered, on paper as anywhere else. A Concurrent arm removes the ordering that bounds a stranded leg, and no delegation loosens a risk control. The requirement text stands, and the row stays PARTIAL on its concurrent clause, citing ADR 0154 decision 5. It waits for a RISK record that brings the forfeited-edge measurement ADR 0154's dissent asks for.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/edge/qip-arbitrage/src/plan.rs::LegPlanner::plan always sorts least-reversible first, and LegPlan::residual_after assumes sequential completion. backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/src/cell.rs::Cell::place_cycle sends whole or rests the slow leg (passive.rs), sizing each leg by the previous fill. A concurrent arm would drop both protections. That is not a tightening, so it cannot be implemented under tightens_only. The row's gap (Lane L24, 2026-10-18) predates ADR 0154 (2026-10-19) and does not cite it, which bar part 4 requires.
decisions.closure: Rewrite the row's gap to cite ADR 0154 decision 5 and this ruling, and keep it PARTIAL; no code.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. plan.rs::LegPlanner::plan sorts by reversibility, and LegPlan::residual_after is the residual-risk measure. Cell::place_cycle and passive.rs exist. ADR 0154 (2026-10-19) decision 5 says 'Legs stay sequential. No Concurrent arm', and its dissent names the measurement of forfeited edge that would reopen it as a RISK matter. The row's gap text does not cite ADR 0154. Refusing a Concurrent arm keeps the stranded-leg protection, and a text-only regrade with the row kept PARTIAL loosens nothing.

decisions.decision: STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL. Closure: the owner obtains venue access and commits the licence record (ADR 0157). Then an ADR amending ADR 0003's feed clause must be accepted before any lane touches FEED_VARIABLE. It decides how a native feed coexists with the simulated venue's fills, where the session credential lives, and what structurally keeps the session order-free. Only then does a lane add the transport into Cell::on_bytes, proven by a recorded-capture decode test with a decoder-field mutation.
decisions.ruling: A native venue feed needs a licensed source and a venue connection, and both come from vendors I have not bought. QIP_VENUE_FEED keeps `simulated` as its only value. The row stays PARTIAL until a licence record under ADR 0157 and venue access exist.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/feed.rs::FEED_VARIABLE accepts only SIMULATED_FEED, and its doc names ADR 0003: a live feed is not a configuration value. The ITCH, SBE and FIX decoders (backend/crates/edge/qip-protocols) and Cell::on_bytes exist. ADR 0157 admits a source only through a committed licence record, and vendor choice is the owner's. This is inbound market data, not an order path, so it is not REFUSE_LIVE, but it is a licence and a vendor.
decisions.closure: The owner obtains venue market-data access and commits its licence record (ADR 0157). Then a lane adds a native transport in qip-edge-node feed.rs feeding Cell::on_bytes, proven by a recorded-capture decode test with a decoder-field mutation.
decisions.skeptic: The bucket is right: a licence and venue access are external (ADR 0157). The closure is not. It has a lane add 'a native transport in qip-edge-node feed.rs' as soon as a licence exists. feed.rs's module doc and its start-up refusal say FEED_VARIABLE accepts only 'simulated', and that wiring a live feed 'is an architecture decision recorded there [ADR 0003], not an environment edit'. They also say the feed is simulated by construction: SimulatedFeed::publish reads only SimulatedDepth, and 'there is no call through which a quote from anywhere else reaches the cell'. A transport added under a licence alone would lift that start-up guard and remove that structural property without the ADR that 10-product-direction.md requires to reopen ADR 0003. It also leaves open how live quotes coexist with fills from the simulated venue's own book, and where a venue session credential lives.

Then an ADR amending ADR 0003's feed clause must be accepted before any lane touches FEED_VARIABLE. It decides how a native feed coexists with the simulated venue's fills, where the session credential lives, and what structurally keeps the session order-free. Only then does a lane add the transport into Cell::on_bytes, proven by a recorded-capture decode test with a decoder-field mutation.

decisions.ruling: Model packs already ride the signed payload, are checked by the cell against the model-pack key, and swap at a pass boundary. What is missing is a model-pack key under ADR 0110's two-person publish, and the second person is a credential this platform cannot mint. The row stays PARTIAL until I name a second approver and apply artefact_signing at deploy.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/src/policy.rs calls ModelManifest::check_releases (backend/crates/libs/qip-contracts/src/policy.rs), so a pack failing the model-pack key refuses the payload. The swap is atomic at a pass boundary (qip-edge cell apply_policy; qip-edge-node control.rs PlanCompiler). backend/crates/libs/qip-contracts/src/reflex_package.rs::PackageSigner has only a test implementation. infrastructure/terraform/artefact-signing.tf's var.artefact_signing is null in every environment, and its HSM keys are unpriced (ADR 0110 'What it costs'), so FUND is unavailable. ADR 0110 decision 4 makes model-pack publishing two-person, and decision 12 records that the one code owner cannot self-approve. The second credential is external.
decisions.closure: The owner names a second approver for the publish environment and applies artefact_signing at deploy. Then a lane adds the stage and health-check step before the pass-boundary swap in qip-edge-node, proven by a_tampered_bundle_is_refused_and_a_valid_one_activates_only_at_a_pass_boundary.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. qip-edge policy.rs:118 calls ModelManifest::check_releases (qip-contracts policy.rs:333). PackageSigner is implemented only in tests (qip-reasoning-engine tests/compiler.rs, qip-deepbrain tests/research_market.rs). The artefact_signing variable's description in artefact-signing.tf reads 'or null for none (every environment)'. ADR 0110 decision 4 makes model packs two-person, with neither credential minted by the platform, and leaves HSM key cost unpriced. A second approver is an external credential and the cost is unnamed, so STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL holds. A small citation slip: 'decision 12' is owner-decisions-2026-10-25 decision 12 (no self-approval). ADR 0110 has no decision 12.

decisions.ruling: Rollout by epoch closes only on a deployed standby. A standby is a second execution node in another zone, which no committed environment enables and decision 5 keeps unbought. The row stays PARTIAL. The conditional-write lease store may be built now, and the root passthrough comes to me as a protected patch with standby_enabled still false.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/standby.rs has only MemoryLeaseStore and FileLeaseStore (single-host). backend/crates/libs/qip-storage/src/gcp/storage.rs already supports ifGenerationMatch, so a cross-zone LeaseStore needs no new dependency. infrastructure/terraform/modules/execution-node/variables.tf::standby_enabled defaults false and creates a second instance group in another zone. No root .tf passes it through, and no patch for it exists under docs/blueprint/lanes, so APPLY_PATCH is not available. The fenced drain (event_fabric/drain.rs::Drain::spawn_fenced) runs only with QIP_FENCING_LEASE, which no committed environment sets. Showing fabricd and ledgerd epoch activation needs a running deployment.
decisions.closure: A lane builds a GCS generation-match LeaseStore in qip-edge-node with a fake-store fencing test and writes the root variables.tf/tfvars passthrough as a lanes patch defaulting to false. The row closes only on a deployment showing a new incarnation fence the old by epoch.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. standby.rs has only MemoryLeaseStore and FileLeaseStore. The execution-node module's standby_enabled defaults to false. No root .tf or environment passes standby_enabled or fencing_lease_path through, and the only lanes hits are triage JSON, with no .patch. Drain::spawn_fenced exists and is wired through QIP_FENCING_LEASE. A deployed standby is required, so STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY is right. One misread does not change the bucket. qip-storage's GCS adapter supports only ifGenerationMatch=0 (put_if_absent), and its doc says 'No conditional writes ... the port has no compare-and-set'. LeaseStore::swap needs a compare-and-set on a version, so the lane must build it with versioned keys through put_if_absent, or argue a port change in an ADR. 'Already supports ifGenerationMatch' is not true as stated.

decisions.ruling: Crypto trades on paper through the same simulated gateway as every class, and its settlement is simulated there too. A decentralised-venue fill's proceeds wait on an operator-declared finality depth, and an order with no declared depth is refused. A bridge is a declared delay and fee on a simulated transfer. Nothing signs, broadcasts or moves a chain transaction.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0155 section 17 keeps backend/crates/services/qip-brokers/src/dex.rs::DexVenue::feasibility_model a model, and asks for a new ADR before any settlement simulator. Its 'Not decided here' leaves finality depth as an operator declaration that delays proceeds. Holding proceeds and refusing an undeclared depth are both tightenings. backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/asset_class_registry.rs registers DigitalAsset T+0 and a crypto spot fills on the simulated broker, but no tokenized-representation or crypto-derivative trade is tested. A real-chain path would be money movement, so it is refused outright. qip-kernel gains no qip-brokers edge.
decisions.adr_title: Digital assets settle on paper through a simulated chain: proceeds wait on an operator-declared finality depth, a bridge is a declared delay and fee, and nothing signs or broadcasts a transaction
decisions.closure: Add the operator-declared finality hold and the simulated bridge transfer on the paper settlement path, refuse a decentralised-venue digital-asset order with no declared depth, and add tokenized-representation and crypto-derivative paper trade tests in qip-kernel tests/asset_classes with the remove-the-record mutation.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. ADR 0155 §17 keeps DexVenue::feasibility_model a model, gives qip-kernel no qip-brokers edge (Cargo.toml has qip-chain, not qip-brokers), and asks for a new ADR before any settlement simulator. 'Not decided here' names chain-finality depth as an operator declaration that delays proceeds. Holding proceeds and refusing an undeclared depth are both refusals. Simulated bridge transfers with nothing signed or broadcast stay on paper. Tokenized and crypto-derivative trades as test inputs match §18's fixture approach. Existing DEX fixtures will need a declared depth. That adds an input and weakens no test.

decisions.ruling: Event contracts trade on paper only. An event contract is a fully-funded payoff bounded to one unit, priced only where the simulated exchange prints it, and settled only on an operator-declared, dated outcome. An unresolved contract is held, never settled at a guess. A prediction-market venue stays without a catalogue record or licence.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/asset_class_registry.rs registers AssetClass::Prediction (T+0, EventDriven among its families), but backend/crates/libs/qip-financial/src/asset_class.rs::InstrumentType has no event type. ADR 0155 section 18 withholds one, citing no catalogue record and no licensed source. Section 19 already sets the paper condition: a price printed on the simulated exchange. The bounded, fully-funded payoff caps loss at the premium, and the outcome record is a declaration rather than a guess. Both are refusals, so nothing loosens. No licensed source is read (ADR 0157 stands). Adding an InstrumentType changes a contract, so it needs an ADR.
decisions.adr_title: An event contract is a fully-funded payoff bounded to one unit, traded only where the simulated exchange prints it and settled only on a declared outcome; a prediction-market venue stays unlicensed
decisions.closure: Add InstrumentType::EventContract under AssetClass::Prediction with the payoff-bound and declared-outcome checks, then assemble one and trade it on paper in qip-kernel tests/asset_classes; mutation: remove the record and assembly refuses it.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. asset_class_registry.rs registers AssetClass::Prediction with EventDriven families. ADR 0155 §18 withholds an InstrumentType, and §19 sets the paper price condition. Adding a paper-only instrument type through an ADR loosens no guard, test or limit. Loss is capped at the premium, settlement waits on a declared outcome, and no licensed source is read. The lane must meet two conditions. First, every risk or margin match on InstrumentType gets an explicit EventContract arm, with no wildcard defaulting it to zero exposure. Second, the committed universe stays equities (§19) until a catalogue record carries a printed price and a sensitivity, so the trade remains a test input.

decisions.ruling: The competing world models the checklist names are the structural models a request declares, and the engine already acts only where every one of them agrees. A federation view is a probability over a proposition, not a simulator, and it stays subtractive under ADR 0125 and ADR 0145 decision 6. No operator route and no TransferGate input are added, because that gate has no production caller and a check nobody calls passes everything.

decisions.ruling: The requirement stands as written, and I will not narrow it to self-contradiction to pass the row. When the platform's own acting constraints are unsatisfiable, the conclusion is Unresolved: its trace and alternates are kept, it is scored in shadow, and it is never queued to be sized. Dissent stays distinct from contradiction, so a contested thesis is Unresolved, not Infeasible. If that empties the paper book, that is what the eligibility rule says, and it is no reason to size what the rule refuses.
decisions.rationale: qip-kernel/src/symbolic_stage.rs::contradictions lists an Unsatisfiable acting step only when the pack finds acting eligible. A contested or low-confidence thesis is therefore Feasible. qip-kernel/src/platform.rs::stage_reason then pushes it to pending_theses, the one road to sizing, and it is sized via Hypothesis::confidence_for_sizing. ADR 0212 decision 1 and ADR 0150 decision 14 decline the 'unsatisfied constraints' clause. Decision 11 of 2026-10-25 holds requirement text authoritative. This adds a refusal on the money path. The dissent test is made stricter, not weaker: it keeps asserting no contradiction and gains 'no proposal forms'.
decisions.adr_title: An acting problem the constraints leave unsatisfiable is unresolved, keeps its trace and moves no money, and a contested thesis is scored in shadow and not sized
decisions.closure: Add Feasibility::Unresolved for any Step::Derived(Answer::Unsatisfiable) acting step and journal it with violated_assumptions and alternates. stage_reason keeps it off pending_theses. Rewrite a_contested_thesis_is_not_a_contradiction_and_still_forms_a_proposal_sized_small to assert Unresolved and no proposal. Mutation: queue an Unresolved thesis.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. symbolic_stage.rs:960-969 lists an Unsatisfiable acting step only when `eligible`. feasibility_of returns Feasible otherwise. platform.rs:15884 pushes the thesis to pending_theses. confidence_for_sizing is at qip-reasoning-engine hypothesis.rs:552. The test at platform.rs:37878 asserts Feasible, a proposal with legs, and sized_on < admitted. Owner decision 11 of 2026-10-25 makes requirement text authoritative. Keeping Unresolved theses off pending_theses only removes a sizing road, so it tightens. The rewritten test still asserts 'not a contradiction', so the existing mutation (drop `eligible &&`) is still caught. ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT is right because it amends accepted ADR 0212 d1 and ADR 0150 d14. Caveat for the lane: 'any Unsatisfiable acting step' must not take precedence over Infeasible. An eligible-and-unsatisfiable derivation must keep its Infeasible mark, its contradictions and its alternates.

decisions.skeptic: All cited facts check out. phase-register.json lists 20 ahead_of_phase entries, and 10 have switch 'none', in phases 1, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15 and 16. Only phase 0 is 'entered', and its row is R12-ARCH-10159. phase_register.rs::every_named_switch_exists_in_the_tree (:149) does `if switch == "none" { continue; }` with no limit. ADR 0143 decision 3 says 'No runtime feature gating is introduced'. Requiring a switch for new capabilities amends decision 3, so ADR first is correct. Decision 11 of 2026-10-25 and ADR 0190:68 both rule out rewording the requirement. A shrink-only list is a tightening, and the ruling turns off nothing that runs in paper. phase_register.rs is not a protected path, and a new ADR file is self-reviewable. One weakness, not grounds to refute: the ratchet only constrains what is written in the register. A capability added to the tree with no register entry is still not caught.

The patch is applied, so APPLY_PATCH would be stale. What remains is a hosted run plus the person's agent-boundary review (owner-decisions-2026-10-31 decision 4). decisions.ruling: The performance gate stays as applied: release profile, one test thread, the 2.0x scaling tolerance and the 10,000 us p99 ceiling, all unchanged. If the hosted runner proves noisy, the answer is to measure it and fix the code or the measurement. It is never to widen a ceiling or to drop the job from deploy's required list. The row closes on a hosted run and a deploy that read it.
decisions.rationale: .github/workflows/ci.yml:303-324 defines job performance-gate, which runs performance and m5_performance with --release and --test-threads=1. deploy.yml:365 requires 'performance gate' to be present and successful. In the lane's runs under machine load, the suite missed twice (2.04x against 2.0x; p99 11479us against 10000us). Hosted-runner noise has not been measured, and only a hosted run can measure it. A wider tolerance would weaken an existing limit.
decisions.closure: Record the first hosted ci runs on main whose 'performance gate' job succeeded, with the runner of any flake, and the deploy.yml run that read the gate.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. ci.yml:303-324 defines performance-gate, which runs `cargo test --locked --release ... --test performance --test m5_performance -- --test-threads=1`. deploy.yml requires 'performance gate' by name. performance.rs keeps the 2.0 scaling tolerances (e.g. :635, :767) and the 10_000.0 ceilings (:2173, :2216). The ruling explicitly forbids widening a ceiling or dropping the job from deploy's required list. That holds the limit, so it is a tightening. 'Fix the measurement' must not become outlier-dropping or best-of-N, which would loosen in effect. The ruling's 'never widen' clause covers this in spirit.

decisions.ruling: This is the same ruling as phase 1. Config Sync and Rollouts are graded against ADR 0114 D4: Argo CD with Config Connector, and the Cloud Run traffic split. I will not write an ADR keeping GitHub-hosted builds, because that would reword the requirement to pass the row. The private pool is built and switched off. It is funded and turned on after dev serves, with its monthly cost named first. The row stays PARTIAL until images are built in it.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0114 D4 limits the control-plane cluster to Config Connector, Argo CD, Kargo and cert-manager, and gitops.rs::the_control_plane_bootstrap_installs_only_the_controllers_adr_0114_names enforces it. R12-CICD-9113 (Rollouts) is BLOCKED by D4, and its capability is R12-CICD-9116. infrastructure/terraform/build-pool.tf and infrastructure/cloudbuild/build-image.yaml exist, and dev tfvars:314 has the pool off. Binary Authorization and Artifact Registry are present (modules/binaryauthorization, modules/registry). Runbook §5 names no pool cost, so FUND_THEN_DEPLOY is not available.
decisions.closure: Regrade the Config Sync and Rollouts text against ADR 0114 D4. Close when a deploy.yml run builds in the dev private pool and Kargo promotes that digest.
decisions.skeptic: Same grounds as R12-CICD-10160, and verified. ADR 0114 D4 (:28-29) limits the cluster to Config Connector, Argo CD, Kargo and cert-manager. modules/binaryauthorization, modules/registry and infrastructure/cloudbuild/build-image.yaml exist. dev tfvars:314 sets the pool false. Runbook §5 names no pool cost. Refusing an ADR that keeps GitHub-hosted builds is the conservative reading, and decision 11 of 2026-10-25 supports it. One note for the closure: the row's check also says 'a manual deploy must be refused by policy'. When the row closes, record that evidence too, not only the pool build and the Kargo promotion.

decisions.ruling: The drift half is in. drift.yml plans dev every day, a drift is a failed run rather than a warning, and no agent may dispatch it. The row closes when a scheduled hosted run plans dev clean, and when R12-SEC-9137's HSM keys are applied so that model activation demands a registry-signed pack. Until then no model is activated unsigned, and nothing is loosened to make the check pass.
decisions.rationale: l9-CICD-8032.patch was applied under decision 3 of 2026-10-31. .github/workflows/drift.yml:36-40 runs on cron '23 7 * * *', and :134-150 plans with -lock=false -detailed-exitcode and fails on exit 2 or on a plan error. scripts/agent-policy.json:50 lists drift.yml as refused to agents. decisions.closure: Record the first scheduled drift.yml run on dev that exits 0. Then close the model half with R12-SEC-9137, once artefact_signing is applied and a signed pack is admitted by model_trust::admit_packs.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. owner-decisions-2026-10-31 decision 3 applied l9-CICD-8032.patch. drift.yml:36-40 sets cron '23 7 * * *'. :134-150 runs plan with -lock=false -detailed-exitcode, and exit 2 or any other non-zero status runs `exit 1`. agent-policy.json:50 lists drift.yml in dispatch_refused_for_agents. artefact-signing.tf has default null with an HSM-only validation at :57, and no environment's tfvars sets it. qip-kernel/src/model_trust.rs:33 defines admit_packs.
