decisions.ruling: Decision 14 of 2026-10-25 stands. RECORDED_DIGEST is a fidelity baseline and the 2.0x ratios are bounds. The row closes only on a committed baseline of relative figures, recorded on a named runner class, with a delta test against it. No file of absolute timings is committed, because it would measure the runner, not the change.
decisions.rationale: .github/workflows/ci.yml:223-239 uploads the replay-bench artifact, and its own comment says 'It is a log, not a delta: a delta needs a committed baseline file, and none exists'. The protected half is on the branch. tick_replay.rs::RECORDED_DIGEST checks replay fidelity, and performance.rs's tolerances are within-run bounds. Neither is a delta baseline. The runner class is not known before a deployment.
decisions.closure: Once the deployment names the runner class, commit relative replay and benchmark figures recorded on it under data/. Add a qip-acceptance delta test that fails when a figure moves beyond a stated band.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. ci.yml:223-239 holds the replay-bench step, whose comment says 'It is a log, not a delta: a delta needs a committed baseline file, and none exists'. tick_replay.rs:328 holds RECORDED_DIGEST. The ruling repeats decision 14 of 2026-10-25 word for word in substance: relative figures on a named runner class, and no absolute timings. The runner class is unknown before a deployment, so STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY is correct.

decisions.decision: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT, same title, with this added to the ruling: the push-triggered plan workflow runs drift.yml's agent-guard step before it authenticates, and it is added to scripts/agent-policy.json dispatch_refused_for_agents. An agent actor or a claude/ branch push never receives the plan-only credential. An agent-authored infrastructure change gets its plan only from a person's push or dispatch, and the required check stays unmet until then (fail-closed). The plan file and its output are not uploaded as artifacts. The plan-only identity is viewer plus state-bucket read, with no write, and plans with -lock=false. drift.yml moves onto it. The row stays PARTIAL until the owner applies the identity and one hosted run is recorded.
decisions.ruling: The pool's refs/heads/ bound stands. A pull request's ref never gets a Google credential, because widening the bound for a plan would hand that credential to any pull request's code. Infrastructure is planned instead on the push to the change's own branch. The plan runs under a plan-only identity that can read state and the project and write nothing, and its result is a required check on the pull request. drift.yml moves to the same identity.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/cicd/main.tf:68 attribute_condition admits only attribute.ref.startsWith('refs/heads/'), so a pull_request run (refs/pull/<n>/merge) cannot authenticate. Widening that condition weakens a gate. drift.yml:32-33 plans as qip-infra-dev and says 'A narrower plan-only identity is R12-CICD-9103's'. ci.yml:614-680 runs only mocked terraform test plans, and infra.yml plans only on dispatch. A new identity and a new trigger change a security contract, so this needs an ADR first.
decisions.adr_title: Infrastructure is planned on every branch push that touches it by a plan-only identity, and a pull request's ref still never authenticates to the pool
decisions.closure: Add a plan-only service account in modules/cicd: viewer plus state-bucket read, no write, plans with -lock=false. Write a protected-path patch for a push-triggered plan workflow on infrastructure/** whose result is a required check, and move drift.yml onto the new identity. Then the owner applies it and one hosted run is recorded.
decisions.skeptic: The ruling, implemented as written, loosens the agent boundary. Today no workflow that authenticates to GCP can be started by an agent actor. deploy, infra, fleet, image, vendor and drift are all in agent-policy.json dispatch_refused_for_agents, with a guard step before auth (drift.yml:63-77). vendor.yml, the only push-triggered one, runs only on main. The ruling adds 'a push-triggered plan workflow on infrastructure/**' for every branch. modules/cicd/main.tf:68 admits any refs/heads/ ref, so every claude/ branch push touching infrastructure would get a Google credential with no person involved. That credential can read the project and the Terraform state bucket, and state holds sensitive outputs (outputs.tf:215). The ruling's own reason for refusing PR refs is 'would hand that credential to any pull request's code'. That applies equally to the branch push that every same-repo pull request is. The cited facts are correct: main.tf:68, drift.yml:32-33, ci.yml's mocked `terraform test`, and infra.yml being dispatch-only. The ADR is still the right vehicle. The guard is what is missing.

decisions.ruling: The SBOM, the scan result and the provenance are attached to the pushed digest with Google's own tooling, gcloud and Artifact Analysis. No new signing tool or action enters the pipeline without an ADR, and a failed attach fails the deploy. The step is written as a deploy.yml patch only after dev's registry answers again and shows it accepts this repository's CycloneDX file. The row stays PARTIAL until then.
decisions.rationale: .github/workflows/ci.yml:418-437 keeps the cargo cyclonedx SBOM as a workflow artifact only. deploy.yml:1067-1125 signs and attests by digest through binauthz but attaches no SBOM or provenance. The registry answered 403 on the last two pushes (owner-decisions-2026-10-31 decision 5). Lane L9 recorded that whether `gcloud artifacts sbom load` accepts this output is unconfirmed. An unverified step could fail every deploy, so the format must first be read back from a live registry.
decisions.closure: After the dev redeploy, run gcloud artifacts sbom load once against a pushed digest. If it succeeds, write the deploy.yml patch that attaches and reads back the SBOM, the Trivy result and a provenance statement, for the owner to apply. Close on `gcloud artifacts docker images describe --show-sbom-references`.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. The ci.yml sbom job (:417-437) only uploads backend/**/*.cdx.json as a workflow artifact. deploy.yml's signing step (~:1067-1130) attests via `gcloud ... binauthz attestations sign-and-create` and has no sbom or provenance step. Decision 5 of 2026-10-31 records the registry 403s. Holding back an unverified step that could fail every deploy, and requiring an ADR for any new tool, is conservative. Making a failed attach fail the deploy is a tightening. No patch for 9108 exists under docs/blueprint/lanes, so APPLY_PATCH is not available.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0118's one project per environment stands, and the per-plane clause is not reworded away. The plane split is created only under an organisation and billing account the owner holds, and only after dev serves from its one project. Moving resources into plane projects then gets its own ADR amending 0118. Until then the resource-hierarchy module stays unused by any root and the row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/foundation/main.tf:14 sets org_mode = var.org_id != null, and google_folder.platform (:74-77) exists only under organizations/<id>. foundation/variables.tf defaults org_id to null, the no-org mode for a personal account. The repository creates no organisation. modules/resource-hierarchy is tested (3 passed) but no root uses it. infrastructure.rs::every_environment_names_a_project_of_its_own already meets the check's per-environment half. The plane half needs an organisation and a billing account, which are external account resources, plus the owner's apply through scripts/bootstrap-foundation.sh.
decisions.closure: When the owner supplies an organisation id to scripts/bootstrap-foundation.sh, wire modules/resource-hierarchy into infrastructure/foundation under an ADR amending 0118. Then migrate one plane at a time, with a real plan for each.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. foundation/main.tf:14 sets `org_mode = var.org_id != null`. google_folder.platform (:73-77) has `count = local.org_mode ? 1 : 0` and parent organizations/<id>. foundation/variables.tf defaults org_id to null. modules/resource-hierarchy exists and no root references it. infrastructure.rs:6944 defines every_environment_names_a_project_of_its_own. An organisation and a billing account are external account resources. Keeping ADR 0118 and requiring an amending ADR before any plane split is conservative, and no billed projects are created. The requirement text keeps its 'and plane' clause, so the row correctly stays PARTIAL.

decisions.skeptic: Verified. execution-node/variables.tf:161-166 admits only c4-highcpu-8/16 and c4d-highcpu-8/16. execution-nodes-enabled.tf:41-46 refuses the flag unless artefact_trust_bundle_file, google_tls_roots_file and certificate_authority are all set. dev tfvars:279 sets execution_nodes_enabled = false. main.tf:754 hard-codes shadow_mode = true. newyork-1's only venue is simulated-1 at 192.0.2.0/24, a documentation range. decisions.decision: IMPLEMENT now, then STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY. modules/network/main.tf is not a protected path. Point data_restricted_vip and engineering_restricted_vip at 199.36.153.4-.7, the same addresses as local.restricted_vip_range. This narrows the reachable API set, so it is a tightening. Add a tftest plus an acceptance assertion that every restricted.googleapis.com A record in infrastructure/ resolves inside 199.36.153.4/30, with a mutation back to .8 shown failing. If a Data or Engineering workload needs an API outside the restricted set, record that in an ADR. Do not leave a record named 'restricted' that points at the private VIP. Keep PSC off until an interconnect exists. The row stays PARTIAL until a real dev plan and the archiver and fabric GCS calls to 199.36.153.4/30 are recorded.
decisions.ruling: Private Google Access, with googleapis.com resolved to the restricted VIP, is the private route, and it meets 'where supported'. The PSC endpoint stays off, because it serves only an interconnect far end and decision 4 declined the hubs. The row closes on a real dev plan showing the private route, and on archiver and fabric GCS calls reaching 199.36.153.4/30 once those are wired.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/network/main.tf:105-136 declares the googleapis.com private zone with restricted.googleapis.com and a wildcard CNAME to it. :274 sets private_ip_google_access = true, as do execution-node:133/816, trust-zones:220 and image-bake:203. modules/connectivity/main.tf:145,161 count on enable_private_service_connect (default false), and outputs.tf:71 says the endpoint serves only a far end's resolver. The check's method is a plan, so it needs a real plan, and qip-fabricd is null in every environment.
decisions.closure: Record a drift.yml or infra.yml plan of dev showing every subnet with private_ip_google_access and the googleapis zone resolving to restricted.googleapis.com. Regrade the 'Enable PSC' gap to 'only once an interconnect exists'.
decisions.skeptic: The ruling misreads the code it cites. It names modules/network/main.tf:105-136 as the googleapis.com zone resolving to the restricted VIP. That zone is data_googleapis, for the Data VPC. Its 'restricted.googleapis.com.' A record (data_restricted_vip, :122-128) holds 199.36.153.8-.11, which is Google's private VIP, 199.36.153.8/30. The Engineering VPC's engineering_restricted_vip (:183-189) holds the same addresses. Only the three-network zone (:218-250) uses the real restricted VIP, 199.36.153.4-.7, which equals local.restricted_vip_range (:306). The requirement's check is 'DNS resolves googleapis to the restricted VIP', and that is false for the Data and Engineering VPCs. data-and-engineering-vpcs.tftest.hcl:112-127 only asserts the record names are non-empty, so nothing catches this. A plan that 'shows the googleapis zone resolving to restricted.googleapis.com' would pass on the name alone. Keeping PSC off and not reopening NCC is correct.

decisions.ruling: Nothing is left to apply: the change-window step has been in infra.yml since b9a45fd5, judging the saved plan before the apply. The row closes on evidence, not code: my approval of the rolling pull request's head, then the first infra.yml {dev, up} I dispatch showing the step's verdict.
decisions.rationale: .github/workflows/infra.yml step 'a core change lands only inside its change window' (:1177, committed in b9a45fd5) runs `qip change-window` (backend/crates/apps/qip-cli/src/change_window.rs) on the same tfplan between 'plan for up' and 'up', so the triage's 'uncommitted in the working tree' is stale. What remains is not code. The `up` dispatch is refused to agents (scripts/agent-policy.json::dispatch_refused_for_agents) and needs billing. Approving the PR head stays the owner's (owner-decisions-2026-10-31 decision 4). No acceptance test pins the step: cicd_governance.rs::terraform_apply_and_destroy_consume_saved_plans_not_auto_approve checks only plan, then up, and a grep of backend/crates/tests for change-window finds nothing.
decisions.closure: Owner approves the rolling PR head and dispatches infra.yml {dev, up}; the run log with the change-window step's verdict closes the row. Meanwhile a lane adds a cicd_governance.rs assertion that the step sits between 'plan for up' and 'up' and judges the same tfplan.
decisions.skeptic: Every claim checks out. infra.yml:1177 'a core change lands only inside its change window' sits between 'plan for up' (:1161) and 'up' (:1197) and judges the same tfplan through `qip change-window`. b9a45fd5's diff adds the step, and `git status` shows infra.yml clean, so the 'uncommitted' triage is stale. cicd_governance.rs::terraform_apply_and_destroy_consume_saved_plans_not_auto_approve checks only plan, then up, and a grep of backend/crates/tests for change-window finds nothing. infra.yml is in dispatch_refused_for_agents, and decision 4 of 2026-10-31 keeps the head approval with the owner. The step runs only on action=='up', so its verdict needs a billed dispatch: STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY is right. The added assertion is a tightening, and cicd_governance.rs is not one of the protected guard suites.

decisions.ruling: Decision 5 stands: I will not buy a Spanner instance to move one histogram, and a single broker's local append timed and called a quorum ack would be a different number under the same name. The series stays on the managed path, proven by its test, and the row stays PARTIAL until a funded managed log runs on a deployed broker.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/apps/qip-fabricd/src/quorum.rs::TimedManagedLog::commit records EVENT_FABRIC_QUORUM_ACK_MS only around a managed log. src/lib.rs::open_managed_log says 'Only Spanner exists'. infrastructure/terraform/fabric.tf has event_fabric_broker null in every environment, and nothing scrapes qip-fabricd. docs/blueprint/lanes/billed-plan-2026-10-19.md item 7 puts enable_spanner at $2,705-$8,140/month for dev. That figure is in neither the runbook nor the row text, so FUND_THEN_DEPLOY is not open. Decision 5 reopens only by an ADR that states a measured need and a ceiling.
decisions.closure: Reopened only by the ADR decision 5 requires (measured need, monthly ceiling). Then set managed_log on a declared broker, scrape qip-fabricd, and record the series moving on that broker.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. quorum.rs::TimedManagedLog::commit (:121) is the only thing that records EVENT_FABRIC_QUORUM_ACK_MS. lib.rs:554 says 'Only Spanner exists.' event_fabric_broker is null in every tfvars, and variables.tf:1770 says 'Null in every environment'. billed-plan item 7 prices enable_spanner at $2,705-$8,140, and dev-redeploy-readiness.md never mentions Spanner, so the cost is not named where the rule requires and FUND_THEN_DEPLOY is not open. Decision 5 of 2026-10-25 is quoted correctly: it reopens only by an ADR stating a measured need and a ceiling. Refusing to relabel an RF1 local append as a quorum ack is the conservative reading.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0119 §3 already decided this: the mirror and its lag series are built and proven now on one host and deployed only at a second region, which stays parked (decision 4). Build the series on two brokers on one host, relax no StreamPolicy refusal for any committed catalogue, and let the row rise to PARTIAL and no further.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0119 (Accepted) §2 names qip_fabric_mirror_lag_records and qip_fabric_mirror_lag_seconds{source_region,stream}. §3 says they are 'built and tested now, against two qip-fabricd processes on one host'. Its dependency section puts the sockets in apps/qip-fabricd and needs no new dependency. services/qip-streaming/src/event_fabric/mirror.rs::plan_copy exists, but no binary runs it. libs/qip-observability/src/critical_paths.rs::FABRIC_MIRROR_LAG_UNBUILT records that nothing writes the series. libs/qip-events/src/event_fabric/policy.rs:453 refuses mirroring ('fabric-mirror is not built'). That refusal is left as it is, so no default path mirrors.
decisions.closure: Add a qip-fabricd mirror role that drives plan_copy from one in-process broker to another. It records qip_fabric_mirror_lag_records and qip_fabric_mirror_lag_seconds{source_region,stream}, with labels bounded by its configured region list and committed stream set. Its test cuts the link and asserts both series grow while the source keeps acknowledging. Deleting the recording site fails the test. No environment starts the role.
decisions.skeptic: ADR 0119 is Accepted. Its §2 names qip_fabric_mirror_lag_records/seconds{source_region,stream} with bounded labels. §3 says 'built and tested now, against two qip-fabricd processes on one host', and the dependency section says 'No new dependency' with sockets in apps/qip-fabricd. mirror.rs::plan_copy exists (:136). critical_paths.rs::FABRIC_MIRROR_LAG_UNBUILT and policy.rs:453 ('fabric-mirror is not built') match. The work is unprotected app code with no deployment, vendor or spend, and no environment starts the role, so IMPLEMENT up to PARTIAL is sound. One caveat for the lane, not a refutation. ADR 0119 §1 says selection is a StreamPolicy arm, not a flag. Keeping the C8 refusal is conservative, but the mirror role's stream set should be the ADR's committed first set, not an ad-hoc flag. Test with two qip-fabricd processes, as §3 says, not only in-process brokers.

decisions.ruling: The requirement text stands: a panel convened on a lost cycle produces new findings and theses, and reading that as existing packages continuing would redefine the row to pass it. While the AI platform is lost, REASON convenes no panel, forms no thesis and records why; installed packages and the edge trade on, and the loss signal stays ADR 0214's Halted or PersistentlyFailing.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/apps/qip-deepbrain/src/node.rs::gate_strategic_service gates only the lattice (platform.lattice_mut().set_strategic_available) on cognition.rs::ai_platform_lost. ADR 0214's 'REASON's narration is not held' paragraph lets the kernel's panel keep producing theses. The 2026-10-31 skeptic REFUTED the row on bar part 4 for exactly that. runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs::place_reason_routing already records a REASON that does not convene the panel when the cost router refuses, so the hold reuses an existing path. A Halted node already refuses orders, so holding the panel costs no trade and is a tightening. Decision 11 (2026-10-25) is the precedent: the requirement text is authoritative.
decisions.closure: gate_strategic_service also sets a panel-available flag on Platform from ai_platform_lost. On a cycle with the flag unset, REASON records a ReasonRouting naming the hold through place_reason_routing and convenes nothing. A run_with test shows a lost cycle journals no new finding or hypothesis and a recovered cycle convenes again. Convening anyway fails the test.
decisions.adr_title: While the AI platform is lost REASON convenes no panel and forms no new thesis, and records the hold as its routing; amends ADR 0214's reading of the deterministic panel (R12-RES-10130)
decisions.skeptic: Verified. node.rs:201 gate_strategic_service only calls lattice_mut().set_strategic_available from cognition.rs::ai_platform_lost. ADR 0214's 'REASON's narration is not held' paragraph reads the deterministic panel's theses as existing packages continuing. The row's gap records the skeptic's bar-part-4 refutation on exactly that. platform.rs:15305 place_reason_routing already records a non-convened REASON on the cost-router and context refusal paths. decisions.ruling: Deploy first: nothing applies infrastructure on a timer while billing is off, and an unattended billed apply is not where a rebuild starts. Once dev is up, the rebuild runs monthly in test, up from empty and torn down in the same run, never in dev or prod; the Fabric half waits until some environment declares a broker.

decisions.skeptic: The bucket is right, but the ruling's plan rests on a misread and pre-commits unguarded, unpriced spend. (1) 'The rebuild runs monthly in test': infrastructure/environments/test/terraform.tfvars has project_id = "unprovisioned", and so does stage. With dev and prod excluded, no provisioned environment can host the rebuild. Running it means standing up a new billed project, and neither dev-redeploy-readiness.md nor the row names its cost. (2) A monthly scheduled up+teardown bills every run, with no per-run or monthly cost named. (3) infra.yml's header makes teardown 'a deliberate human act... dispatched by name' and says 'Nothing here is recoverable once run'. (4) 'Dev cannot be rebuilt from empty: its etcd key has prevent_destroy' misreads runbook §5. That sentence is about turning gitops off through tfvars; teardown takes prevent_destroy resources out of state and `up` reclaims them.

decisions.skeptic: Verified. agent-policy.json sandbox.egress_allow lists only package registries, and its comment says agent-egress.test.mjs fails if a model provider is added. decisions.decision: STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY. Ruling: ADR 0035 stands: one execution node, us-east4, shadow mode. No second or third region is declared or funded until a record supersedes ADR 0035. That record chooses regions from inputs gathered with shadow_mode true throughout: the shadow node's central-plane and inter-region RTT, the venues' published data-centre locations, residency, and a named monthly ceiling. Venue RTT measured over a venue session waits on a separate owner decision to leave shadow mode under ADR 0020/0035, and this row never triggers it. Closure: after dev's one node runs in shadow, an ADR superseding ADR 0035 names three regions with those inputs and a monthly ceiling. The owner then declares them in prod tfvars (protected), and a prod plan shows them.
decisions.ruling: ADR 0035 stands: one execution node, us-east4, shadow mode. The requirement says regions are chosen by measurement, and nothing has been measured yet. The first node is the probe. The record that supersedes ADR 0035 with three regions is written from that node's venue RTT, market-data RTT and residency figures, with a monthly ceiling, and not before.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/environments/prod/terraform.tfvars:20 sets region = europe-west2 and :53 sets execution_nodes = {}. dev/terraform.tfvars:279 sets execution_nodes_enabled = false. docs/adr/0035-one-execution-node-in-shadow-mode.md decides 'exactly one execution node, in us-east4'. Owner decisions 4 and 5 of 2026-10-25 park multi-region and new billed infrastructure. docs/ops/runbooks/dev-redeploy-readiness.md §5 names no cost for a second or third region, so this cannot be FUND_THEN_DEPLOY. The selection inputs the requirement names need a running node to exist.
decisions.closure: After dev's one node runs in shadow and records venue and market-data RTT, an ADR superseding ADR 0035 names three regions with those measurements and a monthly ceiling. The owner then declares them in prod tfvars (a protected path) and a prod plan shows them.
decisions.skeptic: Keeping ADR 0035 and not funding three regions is right, and the cited facts check out: prod tfvars region=europe-west2 and execution_nodes={} at :53, dev execution_nodes_enabled=false at :279, ADR 0035 'exactly one ... us-east4', decisions 4 and 5, and no region cost in runbook §5. The ruling's mechanism is a misread, though. It says 'the first node is the probe' and that the superseding ADR is written from 'that node's venue RTT, market-data RTT'. Its closure says 'dev's one node runs in shadow and records venue and market-data RTT'. In modules/execution-node/main.tf:632, google_compute_firewall.venue has for_each = var.shadow_mode ? {} : var.venues, commented 'none at all in shadow mode'. deny_egress (:553, priority 65000, 0.0.0.0/0) closes everything else. outputs.tf shadow_mode says 'no venue egress rule ... the node cannot open a venue session'. A shadow node therefore cannot measure venue or venue-feed RTT. The only way to meet this closure is shadow_mode=false, which creates venue egress and the venue-credential binding. That eases a step toward a live-order path, and a measurement row must not license it.

decisions.ruling: The requirement text stands, and the row stays PARTIAL. I will not rewrite it so that ADR 0114 D4's refusal reads as a pass. The portfolio brain runs in the kernel on Cloud Run as exactly one warm instance, because a second instance would fork the hash-chained log. So CPU or custom-metric autoscaling is refused along with the GKE pool. The Spanner backing waits on decision 5's measured-need ADR.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/catalogue.tf sets fastbrain min_instances = 1 and max_instances = 1 (:461-462), with the comment that two instances 'would each run the cycle and each append to the same hash-chained log'. deepbrain is also 1/1 (:564-565). decisions.ruling: The requirement names Cloud Trace, and the text stands. Request spans go to Cloud Trace from the process, the way ADR 0121 sends metrics to Cloud Monitoring. There is no collector and no new crate. The exporter is off unless an environment names its project, and a badly named one is refused at start-up. The OpenObserve trace route stays as ADR 0028 left it, unset. The row stays PARTIAL until a deployed qip-api exports a trace that someone reads back.
decisions.rationale: qip-api/src/tracing.rs opens a span per request, and qip-observability/src/trace.rs::Tracer::export already encodes the spans. qip-telemetry-drain/src/cloud_monitoring.rs is the pattern to copy: PROJECT_VARIABLE unset means no thread, require_loopback_egress applies, and TlsHttpClient uses pinned roots. qip-telemetry-drain/src/lib.rs::URL_VARIABLE QIP_OPENOBSERVE_URL stays unset until a collector is vendored and attested (ADR 0156 §5.4), and that collector is billed (ADR 0156 BILLED list). ADR 0028 line 21 records Cloud Trace as the compliant no-dependency path. The NEW_DEPENDENCY tag is answered with no crate (ADR 0109). Switching it on in an environment is the owner's tfvars step.
decisions.closure: Add cloud_trace.rs beside qip-telemetry-drain/src/cloud_monitoring.rs. It pushes Tracer::export's spans on a bounded thread under its own unset-by-default project variable, with the same config refusals and tests. Terraform adds roles/cloudtrace.agent and the egress route, and the row closes on a dev read-back.
decisions.adr_title: Request spans are pushed to Cloud Trace from the process as ADR 0121 pushes metrics, and the OpenObserve trace route stays unset

Tracer::export is at qip-observability/src/trace.rs:229. ADR 0028's context records Cloud Trace as the no-third-party path. ADR 0156 §5.4 keeps the OpenObserve URL unset. Reversing ADR 0028 for traces is an architecture change, so ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT is the right class. No crate is added (ADR 0109), the exporter is off by default with refusals, there is no live path, and no guard is loosened. Two caveats the ADR must carry. (1) ADR 0156's BILLED list counts a hosted collector's ingestion. Cloud Trace bills spans beyond the free tier, so the ADR should name that price and a dev monthly figure before the owner's tfvars switch-on. (2) The egress route must be admitted under egress.rs::the_egress_proxy_dials_only_the_vendor_hosts_the_adapters_named by naming the host in the adapter, not by widening that test. cloud_monitoring.rs:16-17 notes the same gap is still open for monitoring.googleapis.com.

decisions.ruling: This is an external action surface, and it is refused. The SRE agent does not open incidents or pull requests in an outside system. It is given no credential to scale, roll back, restart or drain another service, because that credential would be one more way to change what trades. ADR 0213 stands: the agent journals and drafts the incident, and only a committed runbook acts, only on its own node. The requirement text stands, and the row stays PARTIAL by this refusal.
decisions.rationale: qip-deepbrain/src/operations.rs::runbooks names one runbook (disable_capability research). operations.rs::FOR_A_PERSON writes every other proposal for a person under ADR 0213 decision 2, which says 'Scaling, rollback, restart and drain of other services stay human actions, and this part of R12-OBS-9158 stays unmet'. IncidentRecord is drafted to the operations outbox and never sent (ADR 0213 decision 1). ADR 0114 D8 approves drafting and refuses acting, and D4's reasoning refuses a fourth path to change what trades. The check itself is met by qip-deepbrain/tests/research.rs::a_detected_anomaly_yields_a_journaled_incident_a_runbook_action_and_nothing_else_all_audited.
decisions.closure: None. Drafted incidents stay in the operations outbox for a person, who acts with their own credential. The row's gap cites ADR 0114 D8 and ADR 0213 decision 2 as the standing refusal.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. operations.rs:87 runbooks() has the one disable_capability entry, the effector refuses other actions (:535-537), and FOR_A_PERSON is at :116. ADR 0213 decision 1 drafts IncidentRecord to the operations outbox, never sent. Decision 2 (lines 85-86) reads verbatim: 'Scaling, rollback, restart and drain of other services stay human actions, and this part of R12-OBS-9158 stays unmet'. ADR 0114 D8 (line 59 onward) permits drafting and refuses acting. The test a_detected_anomaly_yields_a_journaled_incident_a_runbook_action_and_nothing_else_all_audited exists at qip-deepbrain/tests/research.rs:703. Opening incidents or PRs in an outside system, or holding a credential that changes production, is an external action surface. REFUSE_LIVE is correct, and the ruling says so explicitly.

That is untrue of the Argo CD, Kargo and cert-manager pods. critical_paths::service_objectives already declares latency, error rate and saturation, and qip-edge-node/src/telemetry.rs::MeshSeries::observe measures the mesh circuit. audit-5-bar.md part 4 leaves the row PARTIAL while a clause is withdrawn. Replace the NOT_APPLICABLE_SERVICE_OBJECTIVES entry with it, and record the measured series read back.

ADR 0036 and its amendment (line 479 onward) vendor Argo CD, Kargo and cert-manager pods, which infrastructure/gitops/bootstrap/cert-manager confirms. service_objectives is at :322. MeshSeries::observe is in qip-edge-node/src/telemetry.rs. Dev gitops_enabled=true, but the cluster is suspended under ADR 0093, so measurement waits on deployment, and STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY fits. Replacing a withdrawal with a declared objective is a tightening. SLOs and GKE system metrics are unbilled. Caveats. (1) Build the objective from free system metrics such as container uptime and restart_count, not kube-state-metrics through Managed Prometheus, which is billed per sample. (2) The requirement reads 'GKE services SLOs'. The latency, error and saturation objectives are evaluated on Cloud Run and Compute Engine, not GKE. Recording the controller-pod series must not by itself mark the row met. Under bar part 4 and decision 11, whether controllers count as 'GKE services' for all four clauses is for the row's final grading, not a reading to pass it.

Autonomous pull-request acceptance and rework are read with the workflow's own read-only token, from the agent markers the guard already reads, so no new credential is issued. The workflow changes are protected and arrive as a lane patch for me to apply. The row stays PARTIAL until the patch is applied and a series is read back.

decisions.ruling: The drafted fixture is the test. An incident record that links a fixture the loop has replayed to the same shift, drafted before any action is taken, is what 'links a new test that fails before the fix' means on a platform where no agent writes to the repository. Committing it stays a person's act under ADR 0114 D8. 'Replay/fuzz/game-day' asks for one of the three, so no fuzz or game-day draft is owed.
decisions.rationale: The question the triage raised (outbox draft or development-process rule) was answered on 2026-10-30 by ADR 0213, so the row's 'current' text ('No SRE agent or incident-to-test pipeline') predates the code. backend/crates/apps/qip-deepbrain/src/operations.rs::Operations::draft_fixture builds a ReplayFixture (journal sequence range, window_digest, platform_sequences, correlation_ids, proposed_test). It drafts the fixture only if operations.rs::replay_fixture reproduces the shift. The IncidentRecord::fixture field links the draft by outbox digest and sequence. With no fixture, every automated action is withheld (outcome="withheld_no_fixture"). main.rs builds Operations::journalled unconditionally. research.rs::each_incident_record_links_a_drafted_replay_fixture_that_reproduces_it holds this, and a mutation that drops the link fails at research.rs:800. No code changes, so nothing loosens.
decisions.closure: Rewrite 'current' to describe ADR 0213's path: incident, then a replay-verified ReplayFixture drafted to the operations outbox, linked from the IncidentRecord, with actions withheld when there is no fixture. Record this ruling in notes and set integrated=true (main.rs wires Operations::journalled). The row stays PARTIAL until a deployed deep brain journals an incident record carrying its fixture link.

IncidentRecord.fixture (operations.rs:197) holds a FixtureLink {digest, outbox_sequence}. At operations.rs:1102-1105 every automated action is withheld with outcome="withheld_no_fixture" when there is no fixture. main.rs:992-993 builds Operations::journalled unconditionally, so integrated=true is accurate. The research.rs:811 test exists. ADR 0213 accepts R12-RES-9087 and states that committing the test is a person's act under ADR 0114 D8, and that fuzz and game-day tests are not drafted. The 'current' text predates this code, so REGRADE_TEXT fits. No code changes and the row stays PARTIAL, so nothing loosens. One small mis-cite: the mutation does not fail at research.rs:800. Line 800 belongs to the test before this one. The test's own mutation note puts the failure at the first link assertion, research.rs:829-832. Fix the line in the notes; the decision stands.

It reopens only by an ADR that states a measured need and a monthly ceiling, after the dev deploy. Neither the runbook nor the row names a monthly cost, so it cannot be funded today.

decisions.ruling: OBS-020 stands and no exception is admitted. A sink that copies the platform's logs into BigQuery so a scanner can read them puts the same sensitive data in a second place, which is the leak this row exists to prevent. Sensitive Data Protection keeps covering the stores its discovery config names. The logs half of the requirement stays unmet and is written down as unmet, not redefined. The stores half is switched on only when its scanning cost is named and funded, after the dev deploy.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/security.tf::google_data_loss_prevention_discovery_config.lake and its inspect and de-identify templates are gated on local.sdp_on. var.sensitive_data_protection is null in every environment. tests/security.tftest.hcl::a_discovery_scan_for_nothing_is_refused holds them. The plan check ('Discovery config/inspect templates exist for data stores') is met in code. backend/crates/tests/qip-acceptance/tests/manifest_wiring.rs::every_workload_identity_may_write_to_cloud_logging_in_its_own_project_and_no_sink_routes_logs_elsewhere refuses any google_logging_*_sink whose destination is not a Cloud Logging bucket. The SDP log sink (db60f078) failed that guard and was reverted in 7ed4be03. Admitting it would loosen a standing guard to pass a row, which the 2026-10-24 record rules out. SDP cannot scan Cloud Logging, so no other route stays inside OBS-020. Enabling the scan edits protected tfvars and bills DLP discovery, and dev-redeploy-readiness.md names no cost for that.
decisions.closure: No code. Record in the gap that the logs half is unmet by decision (OBS-020 kept, no SDP sink) and that the stores half waits on a named monthly DLP-discovery cost, the owner setting sensitive_data_protection = {} in the protected tfvars, and deployment evidence of a discovery run. The row stays PARTIAL.

The requirement's planner, coder, test, security, reviewer, release and SRE roles are the development agents under .claude/agents. Each acts only through a pull request that ci and agent boundary gate, and a release is a person's dispatch of deploy.yml, because no agent merges or deploys (GOV-9067). Phase 9's exit test is named now, but the phase is entered only after phase 8 has exited.
